CP161 consumes the
radiant `EnclRadInfo.radReCalc` value, while CP162 reads the corresponding
`EnclSolInfo.radReCalc`; neither routine clears its flag.

Those producer observations and CP162's consumption have different topology.
`InitSolarViewFactors` normally builds Solar `SurfacePtr` from every stored
Space Surface except AirBoundary Surfaces, including nonrepresentative
calculation Surfaces. `InitInteriorRadExchange` normally builds the
corresponding radiant pointer list from representatives only. Thus CP162's
Solar calculation visits every stored constituent directly and has no
CP161-style representative-area omission, while the shading-change producer
observes the representative-only radiant list. This records an
observer/calculation-domain asymmetry, not a normal unflagged constituent:
`HasShadeControl` Windows are normally made unique representatives. Only a
direct call, malformed or representative-misaligned topology, or a
count/container mismatch can turn the asymmetry into an unflagged Solar
calculation entry. The producer's Solar-count-bound radiant access also
assumes aligned containers and indices. CP162 instead range-scans the entire
allocated `EnclSolInfo` container, so a malformed or reduced count can leave a
retained Solar tail whose flag was not reset or set but is still consumed.

CP162 defines `SmallestAreaAbsProductAllowed = 0.01`. For every stored Solar
enclosure, false `radReCalc` skips all work and preserves both persistent
CP162 targets. A flagged enclosure starts local `SUM1 = 0` and visits stored
`SurfacePtr` order without sorting or deduplication. Every entry immediately
reads the Surface, its current `SurfActiveConstruction`, and that active
Construction. Active `TransDiff <= 0` selects the opaque path and adds

`Surface.Area * SurfAbsSolarInt`.

The area and current inside-solar absorptance are raw. Negative and nonfinite
values flow into the sum. NaN `TransDiff` makes the ordered `<= 0` comparison
false and therefore selects the Window path; positive transmission alone does
not establish a Window class. CP162 performs no local heat-transfer, class,
model, enclosure-membership, active-index, or bounds validation.

Inside the Window path, the declared base
`Construct(Surface.Construction).WindowTypeEQL` selects conventional versus
equivalent-layer handling, even though the path and all optical values are
otherwise based on the active Construction. For a conventional Window, the
routine loops `1..thisConstruct.TotGlassLayers`. Each layer starts with the
active Construction's `AbsDiffBack(Lay)`. Only when the storm-aware
`SurfWinActiveShadedConstruction` array is nonzero can a shade, screen, or
blind substitute shaded optics. Any shade or screen then replaces the layer
value with that shaded Construction's `AbsDiffBack(Lay)`; any blind instead
uses the current low/high slat indices and raw, unclamped
`Interp(Lower, Upper, slatAngInterpFac)` over
`layerSlatBlindDfAbs(Lay)` back-diffuse solar absorptance. A shade/blind flag
paired with a zero shaded-Construction index silently retains the bare active
layer value. Both optical blocks dereference any nonzero shaded-Construction
index before testing shade/screen/blind helpers, so a stale or invalid nonzero
index can fail even when the current flag requests no substitution. A
switchable-glazing flag separately asserts the shaded
Construction index is positive and applies

`InterpSw(SurfWinSwitchingFactor, current layer value,
shaded Construction.AbsDiffBack(Lay))`.

`InterpSw` clamps ordered factors, including infinities, to [0,1], preserves a
NaN factor, and can still create NaN through raw nonfinite endpoint
arithmetic. The ordinary blind `Interp` is the unbounded
`Lower + factor * (Upper - Lower)` expression. All layer results accumulate
in `AbsDiffTotWin`.

`TransDiffWin` separately starts at active `TransDiff`, while `DiffAbsShade`
starts at zero. Under the same nonzero storm-aware shaded-Construction gate,
any shade or screen replaces these with shaded `TransDiff` and
`AbsDiffBackShade`; any blind raw-linearly interpolates current slat endpoints
for front-diffuse solar transmittance and back-diffuse solar absorptance. A
shade/blind flag paired with zero again retains bare active transmission and
zero shade absorptance. Switchable glazing performs a second independent
positive-shaded-Construction assertion and applies `InterpSw` to
transmission. The main conventional contribution is exactly

`Surface.Area * (TransDiffWin + AbsDiffTotWin + DiffAbsShade)`.

No term is normalized or range/finite checked. Shade/screen, blind, and
switchable paths deliberately consume different shaded-Construction members
and current runtime optics through the same storm-aware index.

A positive `SurfWinFrameArea` next adds

`SurfWinFrameArea * SurfWinFrameSolAbsorp *
(1 + 0.5 * SurfWinProjCorrFrIn)`.

NaN or nonpositive frame area skips the branch; positive infinity enters it,
and absorptance and projection remain raw. A positive divider area starts
`DividerAbs` from `SurfWinDividerSolAbsorp`. For a suspended divider, the
active Construction's final layer is dynamic-cast and asserted as
`MaterialGlass`; with its `Trans`, back-beam solar reflectance, derived
`AbsGl = 1 - TransGl - ReflGl`, and
`DividerRefl = 1 - DividerAbs`, the replacement is

`AbsGl + TransGl * (DividerAbs + DividerRefl * AbsGl) /
(1 - DividerRefl * ReflGl)`.

That denominator has no zero, sign, or finite guard. An interior shade or
blind then adds `SurfWinDividerArea * (DividerAbs + DiffAbsShade)` and omits
the divider projection correction. Every other flag adds
`SurfWinDividerArea * (1 + SurfWinProjCorrDivIn) * DividerAbs`. Unlike CP161,
there is no `SurfWinHasShadeOrBlindLayer` gate and no interior material cast;
the suspended-divider glass cast is the third assertion site after the two
switchable-glazing index assertions.

When the declared base Construction is EQL, CP162 uses the active
Construction's `TransDiff`, `EQLConsPtr`, equivalent-layer `NL`, and
`AbsDiffBackEQL(1..NL)`, then adds

`Surface.Area * (active TransDiff + sum(active AbsDiffBackEQL))`.

This branch ignores shading, switching, frames, and dividers entirely. A
base/active EQL mismatch can therefore route active conventional data through
EQL indices or active EQL data through conventional layer arrays; no local
compatibility check repairs it.

Only after every Surface completes does CP162 test the raw sum. Strict
`SUM1 > 0.01` assigns `solVMULT = 1 / SUM1`; positive infinity passes and
produces positive zero. Exactly 0.01, positive values below it, zero, negative

misspelled routine prefix

`ComputeIntSWAbsorbFactors: Sum of area times inside solar absorption for all surfaces is zero in Enclosure: {Name}`.

Only after the warning helper returns does it set `solAbsFirstCalc = false`;
it then assigns `solVMULT = 0`. Subsequent bad sums in the same enclosure
lifetime remain silent. A later good sum, BeginEnvironment, or ordinary
recalculation does not rearm the latch, and a false `radReCalc` preserves both

CP162 has no return value, body-owned container allocation, catch, rollback,

complete implementation is `HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.cc` lines 4473-4644.

`ComputeDifSolExcZonesWIZWindows(state)` at `InitSurfaceHeatBalance` line

Exactly three direct calls occur in one unit-test fixture at lines 3173, 3186,
and 3193. The fixture has three Solar enclosures and two reciprocal 1 m2
Windows whose declared diffuse transmittance is 0.1 and whose enclosure
`solVMULT` values are 1. The first call leaves both receiver

entries equal one plus all three receive flags false. The second sets those

multi-enclosure paths, or either assertion's failure.

CP163 snapshots `NumOfSolarEnclosures` as its matrix extent. Allocation is
controlled solely by whether
`HeatBalSurf::ZoneFractDifShortZtoZ` is unallocated. When it is unallocated,
the routine allocates that square target matrix, then
`EnclSolRecDifShortFromZ`, then the separate
`HeatBalSurfMgr::DiffuseArray` square scratch matrix. It does not
independently verify allocation or dimensions of the latter two objects and
does not resize already allocated state after an enclosure-count change.

Every call then performs this order before inspecting either kickoff flag:

1. assign every `EnclSolRecDifShortFromZ` entry false;
2. replace `ZoneFractDifShortZtoZ` with an identity matrix;
3. replace `DiffuseArray` with an identity matrix;
4. return if `KickOffSimulation || KickOffSizing`.

Thus a kickoff call allocates when needed and destructively resets CP163 state
before returning; it does not preserve a prior exchange solution. With
coherent dimensions the third unit call proves the diagonal/flag part of that
ordering. A partially allocated owner pair or changed enclosure count can
fail during these operations or retain mismatched extents before the later
assertions are reachable.

For the direct pass, write `A(receiver, source)` for the current
`ZoneFractDifShortZtoZ` matrix. CP160 and the daylighting consumer use this
row-receiver, column-source orientation. CP163 visits
`AllHTWindowSurfaceList` in stored order without local sorting,
deduplication, Window-class, heat-transfer, reciprocal-link, enclosure-index,
construction-index, or bounds validation. An entry is skipped when its
`ExtBoundCond <= 0`, when it points to itself by Surface number, when its
declared/base `Surface.Construction.TransDiff <= 0`, or when the receiver
Solar enclosure's `HasInterZoneWindow` is false. The adjacent Surface need
not advertise `HasInterZoneWindow`.

For each remaining entry, the receiver is the current Surface's
`SolarEnclIndex` and the source is the adjacent Surface's
`SolarEnclIndex`. The exact update is

`A(receiver, source) += base TransDiff * receiver.solVMULT * Surface.Area`.

The routine deliberately does not use `SurfActiveConstruction`, a shaded or
storm Construction, or adjacent-surface optics. Repeated list entries and
multiple Windows accumulate. After the update it sets the receiver's
`EnclSolRecDifShortFromZ` flag whenever receiver `solVMULT != 0`; this flag
test is independent of the actual coefficient, area, and accumulated sign.
Both signed zero values fail `!= 0`, while negative finite values, either
infinity, and NaN pass it.

The direct-pass gates are ordered raw comparisons. A NaN `TransDiff` passes
the `<= 0` skip and enters arithmetic; a positive transmittance can still be
multiplied by zero, negative, infinite, or NaN area/multiplier. There is no
range, normalization, conservation, sign, or finite check. The self-boundary
test compares Surface numbers, not Solar enclosure identities. A paired
Surface in the same Solar enclosure can therefore add to raw
`A(receiver, receiver)`, but that raw diagonal addition is discarded by the
following transform because its scratch diagonal starts at one and the pair
loop skips equal enclosure indices.

The pair transform keeps `A` frozen and writes scratch matrix `D`. For
every distinct receiver/source pair it computes exactly

`D(R, S) = A(R, S) / (1 - A(R, S) * A(S, R))`.

For each enclosure `N`, its scratch diagonal then becomes

`D(N, N) = 1 + sum[M != N](A(N, M) * D(M, N))`.

This algebraically folds reciprocal two-enclosure returns into the direct
pair and diagonal without checking denominator sign, zero, magnitude, or
finiteness. A zero denominator, overflow, infinity, or NaN can therefore
produce signed infinity, signed zero, or NaN. The completed scratch matrix is
assigned wholesale to `ZoneFractDifShortZtoZ`; only afterward do exactly two
assertions check its first and second dimensions against
`NumOfSolarEnclosures`. There is no corresponding scratch or flag-vector
assertion, and release builds may omit both checks.

The subsequent flag scan never clears an earlier true value. For each column
`N`, it sets flag `N` true when any distinct receiver `M` has
`D(M, N) > 0`. Under the consumer orientation this is a positive
outgoing/source-column witness, whereas the direct pass set the current
receiver flag. Ordinary reciprocal pairs normally make those sets coincide,
but malformed or asymmetric inputs need not. Positive infinity passes this
ordered test; zero, negative values, negative infinity, and NaN do not.

The final fixed-depth expansion reads only frozen pair matrix `D` and adds
to the already copied target. It requires every visited node's mixed-purpose
receive flag true and all nodes in a path distinct. For distinct
`I, J, K, L, M`, the exact additions are

- two edges: `Z(I, K) += D(J, K) * D(I, J)`;
- three edges: `Z(I, L) += D(K, L) * D(J, K) * D(I, J)`;
- four edges: `Z(I, M) += D(L, M) * D(K, L) * D(J, K) * D(I, J)`.

With receiver rows and source columns these represent the ordered simple
paths `K -> J -> I`, `L -> K -> J -> I`, and
`M -> L -> K -> J -> I`. Each edge gate skips only exact
`D(edge) == 0`, so either signed zero skips while negative, infinite, and
NaN values enter multiplication. Newly added target values never feed later
products. The routine enumerates no path longer than four edges, permits no
node revisit in these multi-enclosure paths, and never updates a diagonal in
this phase. The bilateral pair denominator is the only separate repeated
two-node-return treatment.

CP163 returns no status and emits no diagnostic. It has no catch, rollback,
cleanup, or local topology/numeric validation; its only explicit checks are
the two post-copy dimension assertions. Allocation failure can leave a
three-object prefix. Invalid arrays or indices can fail during reset or the
direct pass. A later failure can leave raw direct coefficients in the target
with a partially transformed scratch matrix, a complete pair matrix in the
target with partial flags, or a prefix of additive two-, three-, and
four-edge paths. A direct retry with coherent arrays starts by erasing all
three objects to false/identity and normally recomputes rather than
accumulating across calls. Kickoff retry instead commits the reset state and
returns. A direct unit or malformed caller bypasses the production
`InterZoneWindow` guard.

When production `InterZoneWindow` is false, the caller does not enter CP163,
so prior target, flag, and scratch values receive no reset and remain dormant
stale. CP159 and CP160 gate their normal interzone-exchange consumers on the
same `InterZoneWindow` value, so that skipped-path state is not consumed by
those normal paths while the gate remains false.

Exactly two direct owners hold CP163 mutations. `HeatBalSurf` owns
`ZoneFractDifShortZtoZ` and `EnclSolRecDifShortFromZ` and clears both by
placement-new reconstruction. The same owner also supplies the surrounding
caller's read-only `InterZoneWindow` gate; CP163 never writes it, and
placement-new restores it false. `HeatBalSurfMgr` owns scratch
`DiffuseArray` and clears it explicitly. Because the single allocation
guard observes only the first owner's target matrix, clearing either owner
alone breaks the assumed all-three allocation coherence: a manager-only
clear can leave the target allocated while scratch is absent, and a
HeatBalSurf-only clear can make the routine allocate against an already
allocated scratch object. Global, Surface, Construction, and ViewFactor
state are read-only dependencies; clearing them does not replay CP163.

Rust models adjacent-zone opaque heat-transfer links and separately parses
window optical inputs, but it has no
`ComputeDifSolExcZonesWIZWindows`, Solar-enclosure receiver/source exchange
matrix or flags, bilateral denominator transform, fixed simple-path
expansion, kickoff reset, or matching failure/re-entry lifecycle. Those
adjacent-zone and optical declarations do not implement CP163.

`ManageHeatBalance` first calls the
`BeginZoneTimestepBeforeInitHeatBalance` EMS point at lines 191-194, then
`InitHeatBalance` at line 198, which reaches CP165/CP164 at lines 2662-2663,
then the
`BeginZoneTimestepAfterInitHeatBalance` EMS point at lines 199-200. CP164

No unit test calls CP164 directly. Exact unit-source searches also find none
of its three material EMS override-on fields, so existing tests assert none
of this routine's global flag, mutable material absorptances, Construction
face copies, last-off behavior, clamp edges, or partial-failure state.

Every entered call first writes
`dataGlobal->AnySurfPropOverridesInModel = false`. Its detection pass then visits
the stored Material pointer array in order, dereferences each pointer, skips
every group except `Material::Group::Regular`, and tests the Solar, Thermal,
and Visible override-on booleans together. The first active Regular material
sets the global flag true and breaks the pass. An active non-Regular material
cannot set the flag. If no Regular material is active, CP164 returns
immediately.

That quick return does not restore any working material absorptance or
Construction face field. Consequently, after a prior active call, turning
off the last Regular override writes the global flag false but leaves the
previous mutable Material and Construction values stale. It also suppresses
the normal non-BeginSim downstream Surface absorptance refresh and the
override-caused Solar/radiant recalculation that consume this global flag.
This is the implemented behavior despite the nearby comment saying
`once yes, then always init`.

When at least one Regular override remains active, the second Material pass
again visits the whole stored array. Every Regular material recomputes all
three mutable properties in exact Solar, Thermal, Visible order. For each
property independently, an active channel assigns

`max(min(EMSOverride, 0.9999), 0.0001)`,

while an inactive channel restores its raw `Absorp*Input` value. Thus one
active Regular material causes inactive channels and all other Regular
materials to be refreshed from input; non-Regular materials remain
untouched. Input fallbacks receive no local clamp or finite validation.

EnergyPlus imports the two-argument ObjexxFCL `min` and `max` overloads,
whose implementation is respectively `a < b ? a : b` and
`a < b ? b : a`. With the exact operand order above, finite override values
clamp to [0.0001, 0.9999], negative infinity becomes 0.0001, and positive
infinity becomes 0.9999. NaN makes the inner comparison false, selects
0.9999, and therefore also becomes 0.9999 rather than propagating.

After the complete Material pass, CP164 visits every Construction in stored
order. `TypeIsWindow` entries are skipped and retain both prior face-field
triples. A nonwindow Construction with `TotLayers == 0` is likewise skipped.
For every other `TotLayers` value, including an unchecked negative one, the
inside material index is `LayerPoint(TotLayers)`. When that index is nonzero,
the routine copies the referenced material's current Visible, Solar, then
Thermal absorptance into `InsideAbsorpVis`, `InsideAbsorpSolar`, and
`InsideAbsorpThermal`.

The outside endpoint is then independently read from `LayerPoint(1)`.
When nonzero, its current Visible, Solar, then Thermal absorptance is copied
to the corresponding Outside fields. A zero endpoint preserves that face's
old triple; a one-layer Construction can copy the same material to both
faces. Endpoint materials are not required to be Regular, so a non-Regular
endpoint contributes its otherwise untouched working values. Negative,
oversized, or stale layer counts and endpoint indices, null material
pointers, and material/Construction topology are unchecked.

CP164 performs no body-owned allocation, emits no diagnostic, returns no
status, and has no assertion, catch, rollback, cleanup, or local validation.
A null or malformed pointer in the detection pass can fail after the global
false write but before any current-material target write. In the second pass,
the group dereference precedes all current-material writes and the three scalar
assignments have no source-reachable mid-triple failure, so a pointer fault
leaves only complete prior Regular-material triples. During Construction
traversal, an invalid layer/count/index or null endpoint can fail before that
face's first Visible copy; an outside-face failure may follow a complete
inside-face triple for the current Construction. Every prior eligible
Construction face remains a complete triple. CP165's completed
runtime-predecessor mutations remain if CP164 fails.

Re-entry while any Regular override remains active overwrites every reached
Regular property from either the current clamped override or raw input, then
overwrites eligible Construction endpoints; it does not numerically
accumulate. Turning off one channel restores it only if another Regular
override keeps the routine past its quick return. Turning off the last one,
or leaving only non-Regular overrides active, takes the stale quick return.
If the outer `AnyEnergyManagementSystemInModel` caller flag is false, CP164
is not entered at all and even the global flag write is skipped, preserving
all prior CP164 state.

Exactly three direct owners hold CP164 mutations. DataGlobal owns
`dataGlobal->AnySurfPropOverridesInModel` and placement-new restores it false.
MaterialData owns the mutable `AbsorpSolar`, `AbsorpThermal`, and
`AbsorpVisible` fields and clears by deleting its material objects and
clearing the pointer array/map. ConstructionData owns the six copied
`InsideAbsorp*` and `OutsideAbsorp*` fields and clears by placement-new.
The same owners supply the read-only guard, group, flags, inputs, type,
layer-count, and endpoint topology. Clearing only one owner cannot restore a
coherent projected state or replay CP164.

Rust retains immutable typed material absorptances and run-blocked
variable-absorptance declarations, but it has no EMS material absorptance
actuator flags or values, `dataGlobal->AnySurfPropOverridesInModel` lifecycle, mutable
three-channel Regular-material pass, Objexx clamp behavior, or endpoint
projection into mutable Construction face fields. Those separate declarations
do not implement CP164.

No unit test calls CP165 directly. Three `HeatBalanceManager` integration
fixtures exercise it indirectly. `HeatBalanceManager_EMSConstructionTest` at
line 1373 repeats `ManageHeatBalance` for morning and afternoon Window targets
and checks current Construction plus downstream solar-transmittance and
daylighting thresholds. `HeatBalanceManager_EMSConstructionSwitchTest` at
line 1974 and `HeatBalanceManager_EMSConstructionSwitchTestCondFD` at line
2181 run through `ManageSimulation` and check only that final current
Construction equals the override value and that its ON flag is true. None
asserts the global flag, compatibility cache, `IsUsed`, active Construction,
no-ON last-off state, ON-nonpositive or OFF restoration, Window cache
overwrite, cached-bad retention, the first-versus-next-call asymmetry, invalid
targets, either CTF/EMPD mismatch warning, either CTF/CondFD source-loss test,
the CondFD node mismatch, HAMT, Kiva, another algorithm, exact diagnostic
counts/order, partial failure, or retry behavior.

Every entered call first writes
`dataGlobal->AnyConstrOverridesInModel = false`, then scans Surface indices
1 through `TotSurfaces` in order and tests only
`SurfEMSConstructionOverrideON`. The first true ON flag sets the global true
and breaks detection. Its integer override value is not inspected, so an ON
flag paired with zero or a negative value still makes the global true. If no
ON flag exists, CP165 returns immediately after the false write.

That no-ON quick return restores nothing. A prior `Surface.Construction`,
`SurfActiveConstruction`, target `IsUsed`, and both compatibility-cache bits
remain stale while the global becomes false. If the outer
`AnyEnergyManagementSystemInModel` guard is false, CP165 is not entered and
even that false write is skipped, preserving the prior global and all other
CP165 state.

When any ON flag exists, CP165 makes a second full stored-order Surface pass.
For every OFF Surface, and for every ON Surface whose integer override value
is exactly zero or negative, the `else` branch restores
`Surface.Construction` and `SurfActiveConstruction` in that order from
`ConstructionStoredInputValue`. It does not clear any Construction `IsUsed`
bit or either compatibility cache. Thus one nonpositive ON flag is sufficient
to enter the pass and restore every otherwise OFF Surface, while turning the
last ON flag fully off takes the stale quick return instead.

A positive override value is used directly as both a Construction index and
the first coordinate of the compatibility cache. There is no upper-bound,
allocation, dimension, topology, or current-Construction validation. The
value is an integer, so nonfinite floating-point behavior is inapplicable.
The target Construction is dereferenced for `TypeIsWindow` before any cache
test. A Window target is always allowed regardless of the Surface heat
transfer algorithm or Surface class. CP165 writes the `(target, Surface)`
checked bit true, then its okay bit true, overwriting even a historical cached
rejection before the cache test, then immediately takes the checked/okay fast
path.

The fast path, whether just established for a Window or retained from an
earlier call, writes `Surface.Construction = target`, then marks the target
Construction `IsUsed = true`, then writes
`SurfActiveConstruction = target`. A checked/bad cache pair takes the nested
do-nothing path and does not restore either current or active Construction;
whatever prior or stale selection is already present survives.

The two cache matrices are owned and prepared outside CP165.
`EMSManager.cc` lines 1849-1857 allocate them only when unallocated with
dimensions `TotConstructs` by `TotSurfaces`, then reset every bit false.
The setup exposes Construction State actuators only for `HeatTransSurf`
Surfaces, but CP165 itself scans every numeric Surface. CP165 neither allocates
nor repairs mismatched matrix dimensions, and the historical key contains
only proposed Construction and Surface, not the current Construction or heat
transfer algorithm.

For an unchecked CTF or EMPD Surface, CP165 writes the cache okay bit true and
then checked true before compatibility inspection. It compares the mutable
current `Surface.Construction` against the target. Unequal `NumHistories`
emits a warning but remains allowed; unequal `NumCTFTerms` independently emits
another warning but remains allowed. The only rejecting CTF/EMPD topology
test is one-way: a current Construction with `SourceSinkPresent` cannot switch
to a target without it. The reverse direction is accepted. After a complete
check, an okay pair writes only `Surface.Construction = target`.

For an unchecked CondFD Surface, CP165 likewise writes okay then checked true.
It compares `ConstructFD(current).TotNodes` with
`ConstructFD(target).TotNodes`; inequality emits a Severe sequence and marks
the pair bad only after that sequence returns. The same one-way
current-source/sink to target-without-source/sink test is independent and can
emit a second Severe sequence before the final assignment gate. A completely
successful first CondFD check also writes only current Construction.

The source emits these exact primary diagnostics:

- `InitEMSControlledConstructions: EMS Construction State Actuator may be unrealistic, incompatible CTF timescales are being used.`
- `InitEMSControlledConstructions: EMS Construction State Actuator may be unrealistic, incompatible CTF terms are being used.`
- `InitEMSControlledConstructions: EMS Construction State Actuator not valid.`
- `InitEMSControlledConstructions: EMS Construction State Actuator not available with Heat transfer algorithm CombinedHeatAndMoistureFiniteElement.`
- `InitEMSControlledConstructions: EMS Construction State Actuator not available for Surfaces with Foundation Outside Boundary Condition.`

For CTF/EMPD, source order is the histories group as one Warning plus three
Continue calls, then the terms group as one Warning plus three Continue calls,
then the one-way source-loss group as one Severe plus three Continue calls.
All three mismatches therefore produce 12 diagnostic calls. The histories
group reports current and proposed Construction names and `CTF timesteps`,
then states that transient modeling may not be valid for the named Surface.
The terms group analogously reports `number of CTF terms` and says the
actuator is allowed. The source-loss group reports the current internal
source/sink, the target's absence, and the exact named-Surface statement that
the actuator is not allowed and simulation continues without the override.

For CondFD, the node group is one Severe plus three Continue calls, followed
by the independent source-loss group as another Severe plus three Continue
calls, for eight calls when both mismatch. The node group reports both
finite-difference node counts before the common not-allowed continuation; the
source-loss group is the same four-call form as CTF/EMPD. HAMT and Kiva each
emit one branch-specific Severe followed by one common not-allowed Continue.
Window, cached-good, cached-bad, restore, and every otherwise-unhandled
algorithm branch emit no CP165 diagnostic.

HAMT and Kiva diagnose before writing checked true and okay false, so a
diagnostic interruption leaves an unchecked pair that can diagnose again on
retry. After their complete diagnostics, later calls hit the cached-bad
do-nothing path. Every heat-transfer-algorithm value outside Window-target
shortcut, CTF, EMPD, CondFD, HAMT, and Kiva remains unchecked, emits no
diagnostic, changes no selection, and repeats that silent no-op on re-entry.

The first successful unchecked CTF/EMPD or CondFD call changes only
`Surface.Construction`; it does not mark the target `IsUsed` or update
`SurfActiveConstruction`. A later call for the same checked/okay pair takes
the fast path and performs all three writes. Switching to a new target checks
compatibility against whatever mutable Construction is current, which can be
a prior override rather than `ConstructionStoredInputValue`; switching back
to a historical checked pair bypasses revalidation entirely. Target `IsUsed`
is monotonic within CP165, and neither restore branch clears it.

CP165 has no body-owned allocation, return status, assertion, catch, rollback,
cleanup, or local validation. Detection failure occurs after the global false
write and before a current-Surface target mutation. In the full pass, earlier
Surfaces can retain completed or first-check-asymmetric results. A Window or
cached-good failure can leave the current write, then current plus `IsUsed`,
before the active write; a restore failure can leave current restored while
active remains old. An out-of-range positive target fails at the initial
`Construct(target).TypeIsWindow` dereference before that pair is premarked or
the current Surface is changed, so an unrepaired retry repeats the same early
failure.

CTF/EMPD caches okay/checked before current-Construction reads and all three
diagnostic groups. An interrupted histories or terms warning group leaves the
cache true and makes retry fast-apply the target; the mismatch itself is only
a warning, although the retry also skips every remaining check and can thereby
miss a later source-loss rejection. An interrupted source-loss group occurs
before its final false write and can directly fast-accept that forbidden
target on retry.

CondFD also premarks okay/checked. A failed `ConstructFD` read, or an
interrupted node-mismatch group before its false write, leaves the cache true
and can fast-accept the node-incompatible target on retry. Once the complete
node group returns, however, CP165 writes okay false before testing
source/sink. If the later source-loss diagnostic then fails, retry takes the
cached-bad path rather than fast-accepting. When node counts match and only the
source-loss group rejects, interruption before its false write does leave true
and can fast-accept. HAMT/Kiva diagnostics instead precede their cache writes.
Child diagnostic counters, streams, SQLite records, and callbacks can retain
their own ordered partial effects. A CP165 failure has no rollback and blocks
CP164.

While any ON flag remains, coherent re-entry restores OFF/nonpositive
Surfaces, rechecks previously unseen target/Surface pairs, and fast-applies
good cached pairs without accumulation. With no ON flags, stale selected state
survives the quick return. Independently of whether any positive target is
applied, a true `dataGlobal->AnyConstrOverridesInModel` disables the
`SimpleCTFOnly && !AnyConstrOverridesInModel` history fast path at
`HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.cc` line 5332 and forces Solar and radiant
enclosure recalculation at `SolarShading.cc` line 10268. The later storm-window
block can overwrite `SurfActiveConstruction` for a storm Window while leaving
the CP165 current Construction intact.

Exactly four direct owners hold CP165 mutations. DataGlobal owns
`dataGlobal->AnyConstrOverridesInModel` and placement-new restores it false.
SurfacesData owns `Surface.Construction`, `SurfActiveConstruction`, and the
read-only ON/value/stored-input/algorithm state and clears by placement-new.
ConstructionData owns target `IsUsed` and clears by placement-new.
RuntimeLanguageData owns and explicitly deallocates both compatibility caches
on clear. Finite-difference Construction data and the diagnostic pipeline are
dependencies or child side effects rather than additional direct CP165 target
owners. Independent owner clears cannot replay a coherent
current/active/cache/use projection.

Rust retains typed Constructions, immutable per-Surface Construction
references, positive-only construction-use evidence, and diagnostic
`ConstructionCtfCoefficientOverride` inputs. It has no EMS Construction State
actuator, mutable current/active selection, historical compatibility cache,
runtime `IsUsed` transition, algorithm-specific acceptance diagnostics, or
matching last-off/failure/retry lifecycle. Those separate facilities do not
implement CP165.

### CP166 `UpdateIntermediateSurfaceHeatBalanceResults` source map

The canonical declaration is `HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.hh` line 132 with a
default-absent optional Zone argument. The complete implementation is
`HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.cc` lines 4951-5020. Its sole production `src/`
call is `UpdateIntermediateSurfaceHeatBalanceResults(state,
ZoneToResimulate)` at `CalcHeatBalanceInsideSurf` line 7812, immediately after
`CalculateZoneMRT(state, ZoneToResimulate)` at line 7811 and at the wrapper
tail. A CP166 non-return therefore preserves the completed inside-balance and
MRT prefix but prevents `CalcHeatBalanceInsideSurf` from returning and, on the
main Surface-manager path, blocks the downstream Air balance.

When `ZoneToResimulate` is absent, CP166 initializes inclusive bounds to Zone
1 through `dataGlobal->NumOfZones`. When present, it assigns both bounds to the
supplied integer. There is no positive, upper-bound, allocation, or topology
validation: zero, negative, and oversized present values each still select
one unchecked Zone index. The sole production partial-resimulation path
normally dereferences that Zone's four lists at `CalcHeatBalanceInsideSurf`
lines 7804-7807 before reaching CP166, so a malformed production argument
usually fails earlier; a direct CP166 call reaches this unchecked dereference.
If an `INT_MAX` Zone body could somehow complete, the loop increment itself
would overflow. An absent nonpositive `NumOfZones` skips all three Zone loops.
Representative mode can still call CP167, whose absent-argument Zone/Space
traversal is also empty, and CP166 still reaches its final global Kiva loop.

Exactly one unit fixture calls CP166 directly, four times at
`HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.unit.cc` lines 8694, 8702, 8710, and 8718. It makes
all four calls with the optional argument absent. The fixture makes the Window
and opaque-or-Window ranges empty, disables representative Surface
calculations, and leaves the Kiva list empty. Its sole nonempty range contains
one opaque Surface. The four assertions check only

`SurfQdotRadSolarInRepPerArea = SurfOpaqQRadSWInAbs - SurfQdotRadLightsInPerArea`

for expected values 0.0, 3.0, -0.1, and 0.00001 with tolerance 1e-10. No test
covers the optional argument, Window addition, multiple Spaces, sign reports
or their energies, stale opposite fields, representative child, convective
assignment, Kiva assignment, nonfinite values, malformed ranges/topology,
re-entry, or partial failure.

The first selected-Zone pass visits each Zone's `spaceIndexes` in stored order
and each Space's inclusive `WindowSurfaceFirst` through `WindowSurfaceLast`
range. A first index greater than the last naturally makes the range empty.
For every reached numeric Surface with `ExtSolar` true, CP166 adds
`SurfWinHeatGain(surfNum)` into the existing `ZoneWinHeatGain(zoneNum)`.
There is no class, membership, duplicate, finite, or bounds check and no local
reset. Non-exterior-solar entries contribute nothing; overlapping or repeated
ranges add the same value repeatedly.

After every Space, including one with an empty Window range or no qualifying
Surface, CP166 classifies the Zone's current cumulative gain. Ordered
`>= 0.0` writes `ZoneWinHeatGainRep` and then
`ZoneWinHeatGainRepEnergy = rate * TimeStepZoneSec`. The false branch writes
`ZoneWinHeatLossRep = -ZoneWinHeatGain` and then its energy. Neither branch
clears the other branch's rate or energy, and a Zone with no Spaces receives
no report write at all. Multiple Spaces therefore publish successive
cumulative snapshots, with only the final successfully reached Space normally
matching the final accumulated Zone value.

Positive zero and negative zero enter the gain branch, as does positive
infinity. Negative infinity enters the loss branch. NaN makes the ordered
comparison false and also enters the loss branch, where negation and the
energy multiplication remain NaN. `TimeStepZoneSec` is likewise unvalidated,
so zero, sign, infinities, NaN, and overflow follow raw floating-point
operations. A sign transition can leave both gain and loss report pairs

`InitSolarHeatGains` normally resets all five direct Zone arrays at lines
2558-2568 before the ordinary parent path. CP166 itself does not depend on or

remains stale.

4985 with the same optional argument. The child copies representative

assignments and later calls, not the already committed Zone total or reports.
A child failure leaves the full first pass plus an ordered child prefix and
blocks every remaining CP166 assignment; retry re-adds the Window gains before
re-entering the child.

The second selected-Zone pass again visits stored Spaces, now using each
inclusive `OpaqOrWinSurfaceFirst` through `OpaqOrWinSurfaceLast` range. For
each reached Surface it overwrites

`SurfQdotConvInPerArea = -SurfHConvInt * (SurfTempIn - RefAirTemp)`.

The prepared range is intended to omit `TDD:DOME`, but CP166 performs no local
class check. The result is per area and receives no clamp or finite guard.
With unchanged inputs, re-entry overwrites the same value rather than
accumulating; infinities, signed zero, overflow, and NaN follow the raw
subtraction and multiplication.

The third selected-Zone pass uses each Space's inclusive
`OpaqOrIntMassSurfaceFirst` through `OpaqOrIntMassSurfaceLast` range and
overwrites every reached `SurfQdotRadSolarInRepPerArea` with the exact tested
short-wave-minus-lights expression. Negative and arbitrarily small values are

Repeated `spaceIndexes` entries or overlapping ranges overwrite the same

Finally, CP166 iterates the global stored `AllHTKivaSurfaceList` without
testing the optional Zone bounds or `NumOfZones`. Each reached entry overwrites

`-(SurfQdotConvInPerArea + SurfQdotRadNetLWInPerArea + SurfQdotRadHVACInPerArea + SurfQdotRadIntGainsInPerArea + SurfOpaqQRadSWInAbs)`.

The five-term sum and final negation are raw and unguarded. During partial Zone

selected Zone can consume a stale `SurfQdotConvInPerArea` because the preceding

and invalid indices or incoherent owner arrays are unchecked.

CP166 performs no body-owned allocation, emits no diagnostic, returns no
status, and has no assertion, catch, rollback, cleanup, or local validation.

first pass, a bad Space/range/Surface/input can leave an ordered prefix of

branch can leave the most recent report lagging the newer partial sum. Each
sign branch writes rate before energy, so its energy can remain old after a
mid-branch failure while the opposite pair was already stale.

The representative child runs only after the entire first pass. Later failure
can leave an ordered CP167 child prefix, then a convective-Surface prefix, then
a solar-minus-lights prefix, or complete all selected-Zone work and leave only
a global Kiva-list prefix. Each reached per-Surface assignment has a single
scalar target; an input/index failure can leave that current target old while
earlier targets remain committed. Nothing rolls back the additive first pass,
so a same-state retry changes its numerical result even when later overwrite
passes would otherwise be idempotent.

CP167 initializes inclusive Zone bounds to 1 through
`dataGlobal->NumOfZones`. A present `ZoneToResimulate` replaces both bounds
with the supplied integer. There is no positive, upper-bound, allocation, or
topology validation. Zero, negative, and oversized present values therefore
select one unchecked Zone; if an `INT_MAX` body completed, loop increment

unchecked dereference. An absent nonpositive Zone count skips the entire

A single outer traversal visits selected Zones and each Zone's `spaceIndexes`
in stored order. Within every reached Space, CP167 executes the HT range, then
the opaque/internal-mass range, then the Window range before moving to the next
stored Space or Zone. There is no sorting, deduplication, Surface-class or

greater than the last is naturally empty and preserves prior target state, but
a malformed 0-through-0 range enters index zero rather than acting empty.
Repeated Space identities and overlapping ranges overwrite the same target
repeatedly.

For each Surface, CP167 reads the raw
`Surface(surfNum).RepresentativeCalcSurfNum` and skips only when that integer
equals `surfNum`. It does not resolve or validate representative chains,
cycles, class, allocation, or ownership. A self representative is a complete
no-op for that range. A non-self chain copies exactly one referenced hop, but
stored traversal order can make that hop already contain a prior CP167
projection; malformed chains can therefore propagate or compound state rather
than converge to a canonical root.

The first per-Space range uses inclusive `HTSurfaceFirst` through
`HTSurfaceLast` range. For every non-self target, it performs a maximum of 21
writes in this exact order:

1. `SurfTempIn`
2. `SurfTempOut`
3. `SurfTempEffBulkAir`
4. `SurfHConvInt`
5. `SurfQdotRadNetLWInPerArea`
6. `SurfQdotRadIntGainsInPerArea`
7. `SurfQdotRadHVACInPerArea`
8. `SurfQdotConvOutPerArea`
9. `SurfHConvExt`
10. `SurfQdotRadOutRepPerArea`
11. `SurfHAirExt`
12. `SurfHSkyExt`
13. `SurfHGrdExt`
14. `SurfTAirRef`
15. conditionally `SurfTAirRefRpt`
16. `surfExtConv.hfModelEq`
17. `surfExtConv.hnModelEq`
18. `SurfQAdditionalHeatSourceInside`
19. `SurfQAdditionalHeatSourceOutside`
20. `SurfTempInTmp`
21. `RefAirTemp`

The first 14 entries are direct representative-to-target copies.
`SurfTAirRefRpt` is not copied: after copying the representative's
`SurfTAirRef` enum, CP167 writes the static report value indexed by that enum
only when it is not `DataSurfaces::RefAirTemp::Invalid`. An Invalid value
therefore leaves the target report flag stale; any other malformed
enum can index the table out of bounds after the target enum has already been
changed. Only `hfModelEq` and `hnModelEq` are copied from the exterior
convection model object, so its other target members remain unchanged. The
source's diagnostic block is inside `#if 0` and is excluded from the build;
CP167 emits no direct diagnostic.

The second per-Space range uses inclusive
`OpaqOrIntMassSurfaceFirst` through `OpaqOrIntMassSurfaceLast` range. Every
non-self target receives exactly this ordered representative triple:

1. `SurfQdotRadLightsInPerArea`
2. `SurfOpaqQRadSWOutAbs`
3. `SurfOpaqQRadSWInAbs`

The third per-Space range uses inclusive `WindowSurfaceFirst` through
`WindowSurfaceLast` range. Every non-self target first computes

`areaRatio = Surface(surfNum).Area / Surface(surfNum).Area`.

Both numerator and denominator are the target Surface area; the representative
area is not read. Any finite nonzero target area, including a negative one,
therefore yields 1. Zero divided by zero, infinity divided by itself, and NaN
yield NaN. CP167 always writes representative
`SurfWinGainConvGlazToZoneRep` and `SurfWinGainIRGlazToZoneRep` multiplied by
that ratio.

Local frame and divider gains each start at zero. A target
`SurfWinFrameArea > 0` branch divides target frame area by the unchecked
representative frame area, then writes frame heat gain, heat loss, inside
temperature, and outside-surface temperature in that order; its local gain is
the newly written gain minus loss. The analogous target
`SurfWinDividerArea > 0` branch performs the same four ordered writes and
local subtraction using the unchecked representative divider denominator.
Ordered positivity rejects zero, negative values, negative infinity, and NaN,
while positive infinity enters. A false branch preserves all four detailed
target fields and keeps its local contribution zero.

After both branches, CP167 always writes

`SurfWinGainFrameDividerToZoneRep = frameHeatGain + dividerHeatGain`

and then

`SurfWinHeatGain = (representative SurfWinHeatGain - representative SurfWinGainFrameDividerToZoneRep * areaRatio) + target SurfWinGainFrameDividerToZoneRep`.

Thus two false area branches preserve eight detailed frame/divider fields but
overwrite the combined target aggregate with zero and still recompute whole
Window heat gain. Zero representative denominators, nonfinite ratios,
subtractions, products, sums, and overflow are all unguarded. Representative
chains and repeat calls can consume a previously projected Window as the next
source and compound these scalings.

CP167 has no body-owned allocation, status return, enabled assertion, catch,
rollback, cleanup, finite check, or local validation. Failure in the current
Space's HT range can leave any ordered scalar prefix for the current target;
notably, `SurfTAirRef` can be committed before a failed report lookup. After
that range completes, the opaque range can leave a prefix of its triple. After
both complete, the Window range can leave the two glazing writes, a frame or
divider prefix, and the aggregate write before the final whole-Window write.
Only after all three ranges complete does traversal advance to the next stored
Space or Zone, so an earlier Space can own a complete HT/opaque/Window prefix
while a later one remains partial or untouched. A coherent retry overwrites
every field it reaches from current representative inputs, but self,
false-branch, empty, inverted, no-longer-reached, and Invalid report cases
preserve stale state. Traversal-dependent chains can make even otherwise
overwrite-shaped retry results differ.

reconstruct the representative projection.

The canonical declaration is `HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.hh` lines 140-141
with a default-absent optional Zone argument. The complete implementation is
`HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.cc` lines 5583-5699. Its only production `src/`

One `SurfaceGeometry.unit.cc` fixture calls CP168 directly three times with
the optional argument absent, at lines 5907, 5924, and 5948. With all five
heat-transfer Surface temperatures at 10, the first call checks all three Zone
MRTs and both enclosure MRTs at 10 plus each Space equal to its enclosure. The
second changes the three Zones' Surface temperatures to 10, 20, and 30 and
checks those Zone MRTs, enclosure MRTs 16.667 and 20, and the Space copies.
Before the third, it zeros all five heat-transfer Surface areas, assigns Zone
MATs 20, 25, and 28 and Space MATs 15, 22, and 28, manually rearms
`CalculateZoneMRTfirstTime`, and checks Zone MAT fallback plus low-AE
enclosure results 21.5 and 22 derived from Space MATs. The fixture does not
assert Space Volume or which volume subbranch executes, and these expected
outputs do not independently distinguish the strict volume-weighted branch
from the arithmetic fallback. It does not assert warnings and does not cover a
present optional Zone, cache staleness, exact thresholds, nonfinite values,
invalid topology, partial failure, or retry.

While `CalculateZoneMRTfirstTime` is true, CP168 calls
`SurfaceAE.allocate(TotSurfaces)` and `ZoneAESum.allocate(NumOfZones)`, zeros
both arrays, and zeros every stored radiant enclosure's `sumAE`. It then visits
numeric Surfaces 1 through `TotSurfaces`. Only `HeatTransSurf` entries receive

`SurfaceAE = Area * Construct(Construction).InsideAbsorpThermal`.

The same raw value is added to `ZoneAESum(Zone)` only when `Zone > 0` and to
`EnclRadInfo(RadEnclIndex).sumAE` only when `RadEnclIndex > 0`. These are
positive-only index gates, not upper-bound or topology checks. Construction,
array, and pointer validity, area and absorptance signs, and finiteness are
unchecked. Non-heat-transfer entries retain zero cache values.

First-time cache construction is global even for a present optional Zone. The
flag stays true throughout the entire routine and becomes false only at the
successfully reached final line 5698. Its production rearm is
HeatBalSurfMgr's explicit clear; the unit fixture also rearms it manually.
Later changes to Surface count, Zone count, area, Construction,
`InsideAbsorpThermal`, heat-transfer membership, Zone, or radiant-enclosure
topology therefore leave cached values and dimensions stale until rearmed.

Applicability is established next. With a present `ZoneToResimulate`, CP168
directly dereferences that raw Zone, visits its stored `spaceIndexes`, reads
each Space's `radiantEnclosureNum`, then writes that enclosure's `sumAET = 0`
followed by `reCalcMRT = true`. There is no positive or upper-bound check and
duplicates repeat the pair. With the optional argument absent, CP168 sets
`reCalcMRT = true` for every stored enclosure but does not pre-zero `sumAET`.
The routine never sets a recalculation flag false, and no other source writer
does so. Flags are therefore monotonic until ViewFactor state is cleared.

This flag lifecycle makes partial recalculation nonlocal. A first partial call
marks the selected Zone's Space enclosures, but each marked enclosure later
uses its complete global `SurfacePtr` and writes every listed Space MRT,
including Spaces outside the selected Zone in a shared enclosure. After any
full call, every flag remains true, so later partial calls recalculate every
enclosure. A selected Zone with no Spaces sets no new flag, although stale true
flags can still cause global enclosure work.

The Zone loop always scans numeric Zones 1 through `NumOfZones` and skips a
Zone only when a present optional value differs. It takes the corresponding
`zoneHeatBalance` record before testing the cached denominator. A strict
`ZoneAESum(ZoneNum) > 0.01` enters the weighted branch. That branch starts a
local `zoneSumAET` at zero, follows stored Spaces and each inclusive
`HTSurfaceFirst` through `HTSurfaceLast` range, and for every reached numeric
Surface computes

`surfAET = SurfaceAE(SurfNum) * SurfTempIn(SurfNum)`.

It adds `surfAET` to the local Zone numerator and also unconditionally indexes
`EnclRadInfo(Surface(SurfNum).RadEnclIndex).sumAET` and adds the same value.
Unlike first-time `sumAE` construction, this enclosure access has no positive
index gate. After all stored ranges complete, CP168 writes

`Zone.MRT = zoneSumAET / ZoneAESum(ZoneNum)`.

A cached denominator not strictly greater than 0.01 takes the fallback,
including exactly 0.01, negative values, and NaN. While first-time remains
true, CP168 emits one Warning followed by one Continue diagnostic stating that
the Zone's area-times-emissivity sum is zero and MRT will use MAT. It then
writes the Zone's own `MAT` to `MRT`. Later fallback calls are silent.

The enclosure loop is global and follows stored `EnclRadInfo` order, skipping
only records whose monotonic `reCalcMRT` is false. A strict `sumAE > 0.01`
branch first resets `sumAET` to zero, then follows the enclosure's complete
stored `SurfacePtr` list and accumulates

`sumAET += SurfaceAE(surfNum) * SurfTempIn(surfNum)`,

before writing `MRT = sumAET / sumAE`. This reset and recomputation discard
any `sumAET` additions made by the preceding Zone loop.

An enclosure denominator not strictly greater than 0.01 preserves its current
`sumAET`. While first-time remains true it emits one Warning followed by one
Continue diagnostic stating that the enclosure's area-times-emissivity sum is
zero and MRT will use volume-weighted MAT. It then visits every stored
`spaceNums` entry and accumulates raw `Volume`, `Space.MAT * Volume`, and
`Space.MAT`. Strict `sumVol > 0.01` writes `sumMATVol / sumVol`; otherwise it
writes `sumMAT / (int)spaceNums.size()`. There is no empty-list or narrowing
cast guard. After either enclosure branch, CP168 copies the enclosure MRT to
every stored Space MRT in list order.

All traversal is raw. Duplicate Spaces, Surface ranges, `SurfacePtr` entries,
or `spaceNums` repeat additions or writes. Empty and inverted HT ranges
naturally preserve the local numerator contribution; malformed 0-through-0
ranges enter index zero. Numerators can disagree with stale cached
denominators after topology or property changes. Zone-associated Surface
weights can also be added to a different or invalid radiant enclosure.

Exact 0.01 denominators and volume sums fall back. Positive infinity passes
the ordered threshold, while negative infinity and NaN fall back. Products,
sums, ratios, MAT, Volume, area, absorptance, temperatures, overflow, signed
zero, infinities, and NaN are never clamped or normalized. A positive-infinite
volume sum can produce infinity divided by infinity; a NaN volume sum takes
the arithmetic fallback; an empty fallback enclosure divides zero by an
integer zero.

CP168 has no status return, enabled assertion, catch, rollback, cleanup, or
local validation. First-time failure can leave an allocation/zero prefix,
complete earlier enclosure `sumAE` clears, and a Surface-cache prefix whose
current `SurfaceAE` may be written before a bad Zone or enclosure add fails.
A present optional failure can leave earlier `sumAET`-then-`reCalcMRT` pairs;
an absent call can leave a flag prefix. Zone work can leave enclosure
`sumAET` additions before the current Zone MRT is committed. Fallback
diagnostics can leave a Warning without its Continue or either diagnostic
before the MRT write.

Enclosure failure can leave a positive-branch reset/add prefix, an enclosure
MRT without all Space MRT copies, or a fallback diagnostic/local-read prefix.
The final first-time flag clear occurs only after all work succeeds. A failed
first-time retry rebuilds and rewarns but does not globally reset `sumAET`,
`reCalcMRT`, or prior MRT values; a positive enclosure resets its own
`sumAET`, whereas fallback preserves it. Failure after a prior successful call
reuses potentially stale caches and makes later fallback warnings silent.

Exactly three direct owners hold CP168 mutations. HeatBalSurfMgr owns
`SurfaceAE`, `ZoneAESum`, and `CalculateZoneMRTfirstTime` and clears them
explicitly, rearming the flag. ViewFactorInfoData owns enclosure `sumAE`,
`sumAET`, `MRT`, and `reCalcMRT`; its explicit clear removes the enclosure
records whose defaults are zero/false. ZoneTempPredictorCorrectorData owns Zone
and Space `MRT` fields and clears by placement-new. Warning counters, streams,
callbacks, and SQLite records are diagnostic child side effects. Independent
owner clears cannot replay a coherent cache/MRT projection.

Rust has bounded per-Surface area, inside thermal absorptance, and inside

cache topology, monotonic recalculation flags, MAT fallback lifecycle,

from these three newly projected components.

### CP172 `CalcHeatBalanceInsideSurf2` source map

CP172 maps required general `CalcHeatBalanceInsideSurf2`, declared at

The four `const std::vector<int> &` arguments independently define CP172's
work topology. `HTSurfs` drives reference-air setup, the EMPD/HAMT prepass,
temperature/history/report commits and limit checks;
`IZSurfs` drives paired outside-temperature synchronization;
`HTNonWindowSurfs` drives opaque solves, convergence differences, and the
post-loop moisture update; and `HTWindowSurfs` drives Window resets and solves.
The optional Zone does not select, filter, or validate any of those vectors
inside CP172. Its only body uses are forwarding to
`CalcInteriorRadExchange` at line 7929 and `InitIntConvCoeff` at line 7946.
There is no list consistency, Zone membership, Surface class, sort,
deduplication, pair, representative, dimension, or bounds validation.
Malformed and overlapping vectors can therefore omit, repeat, or apply
different phases to the same raw index; direct callers can provide topology
that disagrees with the optional Zone. A non-window-only index can be solved
and convergence-tested without the HT commit/check, while an HT-only index
can commit/check a stale unsolved temperature. Duplicate non-window entries
repeat solve work and their moisture-tail terms add again to the same raw Zone.

Before convergence, CP172 performs these ordered mutations:

1. It visits `HTSurfs`, skips only current-class `TDD_Dome`, obtains each
   Surface's inside reference-air temperature, and writes both
   `RefAirTemp(SurfNum)` and `SurfTempEffBulkAir(SurfNum)`.
2. It visits every `HTWindowSurfs` entry and unconditionally zeros exactly 13
   selected fields: `SurfWinHeatGain`, `SurfWinHeatGainRep`,
   `SurfWinHeatLossRep`, `SurfWinGainConvGlazToZoneRep`,
   `SurfWinGainIRGlazToZoneRep`, `SurfWinLossSWZoneToOutWinRep`,
   `SurfWinGainFrameDividerToZoneRep`, `SurfWinGainConvShadeToZoneRep`,
   `SurfWinGainIRShadeToZoneRep`, `SurfWinFrameQRadOutAbs`,
   `SurfWinFrameQRadInAbs`, `SurfWinDividerQRadOutAbs`, and
   `SurfWinDividerQRadInAbs`.
3. It resets global `InsideSurfIterations` to zero, then samples every stored
   `allInsideSourceSurfaceList` Schedule into
   `SurfQAdditionalHeatSourceInside`, even for a partial-Zone call.
4. When `AnyKiva`, not warmup, and either the Kiva timestep mode is
   `TIMESTEP` or it is `HOURLY` at `TimeStep == 1`, it advances all Kiva
   instances through `calcKivaInstances`.

`Converged` starts false, so every entered call attempts at least one pass.
Each pass first assigns the complete `SurfTempIn` array to
`SurfTempInsOld`, including entries outside a partial list. When `AnyKiva`, it
then visits the complete Kiva `surfaceMap`, temporarily writes every mapped
`SurfTempIn` from `results.Trad - Kelvin`, calls interior long-wave exchange,
and only after that child returns visits the complete map again to restore
from `SurfTempInsOld`. Inside convection is refreshed only when the
pre-increment `InsideSurfIterations` is positive and divisible by 30. A run
that reaches the hard limit therefore refreshes at counts 30, 60, through 480,
before passes 31, 61, through 481; it does not refresh before pass 1 or pass
501.

An `AnyEMPD || AnyHAMT` prepass next visits `HTSurfs`, again skips current-class
TDD domes, and for EMPD/HAMT entries establishes `HConvInFD`, vapor-air
density, and mass-convection state from the Surface's raw Zone. The
representative-filtered `HTNonWindowSurfs` pass then selects adiabatic versus
standard/interzone equations and CTF, EMPD, CondFD, HAMT, or Kiva handling.
Its branches include pool terms, embedded construction sources, mixed-model
CTF temperature limits, radiant-system inside/outside coefficients and
interzone coefficient pairing, and interior movable insulation. The Kiva
branch reads `kivaManager.surfaceMap[SurfNum]`; a missing key can therefore be
inserted before its default result is consumed. Interior movable insulation
combined with an embedded source or sink emits the ordered severe/continue
messages and fatally terminates at lines 8265-8278.

The representative-filtered `HTWindowSurfs` pass solves TDD diffusers on every
iteration, including their heat-gain report components, while a regular
Window executes only when the pre-increment count is zero. That first-pass
branch selects user, wind/rain, no-wind, or interzone exterior convection,
resolves shading or equivalent-layer emissivity, calls
`Window::CalcWindowHeatBalance`, and commits its inside temperature. The
following `HTSurfs` pass always writes inside history and outside report
temperature before the original-class TDD gates. A TDD diffuser then uses
inside-out chained assignments to update its Dome's inside fields and another
chain to couple Dome/diffuser outside fields. CP172 invokes the CP174-mapped
shared required surface-temperature checker on ordinary entries outside the
normal limits, then `IZSurfs` copies each raw paired inside-history value into both current
outside report temperature and outside-history term 1. Only after these
writes does it increment `InsideSurfIterations`.

Convergence takes the maximum absolute current-versus-snapshot change across

`AnyCondFD`, rather than the supplied subset, selects
`MaxAllowedDelTempCondFD` and the global CondFD relaxation lifecycle;
otherwise `MaxAllowedDelTemp` applies. The CondFD factor resets to its input on
pass one and, after `IterationsForCondFDRelaxChange`, multiplies by 0.9 while
unconverged with a 0.1 floor. `MinIterations` can clear an otherwise true
convergence result. The hard-limit test is later and strictly
`InsideSurfIterations > MaxIterations`, where `MaxIterations` is 500, so the
limit path completes 501 passes. Outside warmup it increments the persistent
nonconvergence count, emits direct warnings for counts below 16 and recurring
warnings thereafter, then breaks. The break also occurs during warmup without
that warning. Because the limit test is independent of the current
`Converged` value, it still warns outside warmup and breaks if pass 501 is the
first pass to satisfy the tolerance.

After the loop, `AnyEMPD || AnyHAMT` first zeros `SumHmAW`, `SumHmARa`, and

then visits only the supplied `HTNonWindowSurfs`: HAMT entries call

terms. A partial CP172 call can therefore erase moisture contributions for

whole-array snapshot, Kiva advance/substitution, global iteration and CondFD
factor, paired radiant coefficients, TDD counterpart writes, diagnostics, and

The Zone detail block is additionally guarded by the shared

gain in W on this ordinary path. Exact AFN control

During warmup, crossing the before-fatal limit is not itself fatal. Only

### CP175 `CalcOutsideSurfTemp` source map

CP175 maps required `CalcOutsideSurfTemp`, declared at
`HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.hh` lines 195-202 and implemented at
`HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.cc` lines 9470-9763. Its only direct production
caller is `CalcHeatBalanceOutsideSurf`, at line 7355 in
`OtherSideCoefCalcExt`, line 7419 in `OtherSideCondModeledExt`, and line 7626
in `ExternalEnvironment`. The first two calls admit only CTF or EMPD and
retain the parent’s zero `HMovInsul`; the modeled-other-side call follows the CP176-mapped
line-7416 `CalcExteriorVentedCavity` update. The exterior call admits CTF,
EMPD, or a TDD dome and is the only path that samples exterior movable
insulation. EcoRoof has already continued at line 7440.

The reusable parent can be reached by the canonical full-building call and by
several full or optional-Zone recalculation entrypoints. It traverses numeric
Zone order, stored Space order, and inclusive heat-transfer-Surface ranges,
skips Windows, and under optional resimulation skips a Surface unrelated to
the requested or adjacent Zone. Ground, F-factor ground, no-calc other-side
coefficient, Kiva, and interior/interzone routes do not call CP175. Ordinary
CondFD and HAMT exterior Surfaces also bypass it; the explicit TDD-dome class
alternative is admitted independently of the algorithm field. One parent-local `MovInsulErrorFlag` is initialized false before the
traversal. Each of the three calls is immediately followed by a flag check
and Fatal, so a flagged return prevents the current Surface’s later CP171
common-tail convection store.

Every entered call preserves this prologue order:

1. strict `HMovInsul > 0.0` selects movable insulation;
2. raw Surface and Construction references are bound;
3. strict `CTFCross[0] > 0.01` selects quick conduction and computes
   `F1 = CTFCross[0] / (CTFInside[0] + SurfHConvInt)`; equality, negatives,
   and NaN select slow conduction;
4. sky defaults to global `SkyTemp`, ground defaults to global
   `OutDryBulbTemp`, and surrounding temperature defaults to zero;
5. an enabled surrounding-Surface property may sample sky and ground
   schedules and uses the Surface’s precomputed `SrdSurfTemp`; an enabled
   ground-Surface-temperature property then overwrites ground last, winning
   over a surrounding-property ground schedule;
6. `SurfOutsideTempHist(1)(SurfNum)` is bound as `TH11` before the exhaustive
   temperature branch.

For compact formula boundaries, let `Co` and `Ci` be the outside and inside
CTF constant parts, `Cx` the cross coefficient, `So` and `Si` the absorbed
outside and inside shortwave terms, `Qsrc` source history, and define:

```text
E = (Hconv + Hair)*Text + Qadditional
    + Hsky*Tsky + Hground*Tground + Hsrd*Tsrd
I = Ci + Si + QradInternal + Hinside*MAT + QnetInsideLW
```

A TDD dome wins before all movable/quick combinations. It indexes the raw
pipe, diffuser, and diffuser Space, calculates `Ueff = 1 / Reff`, replaces F1
with `Ueff / (Ueff + Hinside_diffuser)`, and writes:

```text
(dome layer-1 SW / 2 + E
 + F1*(diffuser layer-1 SW / 2 + diffuser radiant gain
       + Hinside_diffuser*MAT_diffuser + diffuser net inside LW))
/ (Ueff + Hconv + Hair + Hsky + Hground + Hsrd - F1*Ueff)
```

No embedded-source term appears in that temperature equation.

Without movable insulation, `OSCMPtr == 0` selects the separated
environmental equations. Slow conduction writes:

```text
(-Co + So + E + Cx*Tin [+ CTFSourceOut*Qsrc])
/ (CTFOutside + Hconv + Hair + Hsky + Hground + Hsrd)
```

Quick conduction replaces `Cx*Tin` with `F1*I` and subtracts `F1*Cx`
from the denominator. Its source case adds `CTFSourceOut*Qsrc` but,
notably, does not add `CTFSourceIn*Qsrc` inside the F1 term.

Any nonzero `OSCMPtr`, including a malformed negative value, instead indexes
raw `TRad` and `HRad`. The slow equation is:

```text
(-Co + Hconv*Text + Qadditional + HRad*TRad + Cx*Tin
 [+ CTFSourceOut*Qsrc]) / (CTFOutside + Hconv + HRad)
```

The quick OSCM equation again substitutes the F1-scaled inside balance and
subtracts `F1*Cx`; unlike the quick no-OSCM source case, it includes
`CTFSourceIn*Qsrc` inside that coupled term. OSCM equations exclude exterior
solar, `Hair`, sky, ground, and surrounding forcing even though schedule and
property lookups already occurred.

Movable-insulation branches ignore OSCM radiation. Both calculate:

```text
F2 = Hmov / (Hmov + Hconv + Hair + Hsky + Hground + Hsrd)
M  = movable-insulation SW + E
```

The slow result is `(-Co + So + Cx*Tin + F2*M) /
(CTFOutside + Hmov - F2*Hmov)`. The quick result replaces the direct cross
term with `F1*I` and additionally subtracts `F1*Cx` from the denominator.
Neither equation includes embedded-source terms; that combination is
rejected only after the temperature and reporting writes.

After the selected branch commits `TH11`, CP175 computes and stores:

```text
SurfQdotRadOutRepPerArea =
  -(Hsky*(TH11 - Tsky) + Hair*(TH11 - Text)
    + Hground*(TH11 - Tground) + Hsrd*(TH11 - Tsrd))
```

This report intentionally excludes `SurfHConvExt` and does not consume the
parent-computed nonlinear `SurfQRadLWOutSrdSurfs`. It uses the same standard
coefficients even when the temperature came from an OSCM equation.

When `SourceSinkPresent && MovInsulPresent`, outside history and the radiant
report are already committed. CP175 emits one Severe and three Continue
lines, including a raw exterior-insulation material lookup, then sets the
caller-owned flag true and returns. Because the flag write is last, output,
formatting, or material failure can leave a diagnostic prefix with the flag
still false. None of the three radiant-system coefficients is touched, and
the production parent fatals before CP171. CP175 never clears a preexisting
true flag on any successful path.

For an embedded source without movable insulation, CP175 calculates
`RadSysDiv` with `CTFOutside + Hconv + Hair + Hsky + Hground + Hsrd + Hsrd`:
the surrounding coefficient is duplicated in the source. It then overwrites
`RadSysToHBConstCoef`, `RadSysToHBTinCoef`, and
`RadSysToHBQsrcCoef` in that order. The constant numerator omits
`SurfQAdditionalHeatSourceOutside`, and these generic standard-environment
coefficients are used regardless of the temperature branch. A non-source
call does not clear any prior coefficient.

`HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.unit.cc` lines 95-186 contain the sole literal

Five fixtures call the parent directly. The calls at lines 1925, 2489, 3067,

successful coefficient writes, the duplicated divisor, an input-true flag,
malformed topology, nonfinite arithmetic, partial failure, or retry.

CP175 has no finite, sign, denominator, dimension, index, topology, CTF-array,
schedule-value, property, TDD, Space, or material validation, no return value
or status normalization beyond the caller-owned `ErrorFlag`, and no assertion, catch,

`HMovInsul == 0` is absent, `CTFCross[0] == 0.01` is slow, and NaN fails both

A failure while binding inputs or `TH11`, or while evaluating the selected

### CP176 `CalcExteriorVentedCavity` source map

CP176 maps non-required `CalcExteriorVentedCavity`, declared at
`HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.hh` line 204 and implemented at
`HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.cc` lines 9765-9850. Its only direct
production caller is `CalcHeatBalanceOutsideSurf`, at line 7416 in
the `OtherSideCondModeledExt` CTF/EMPD branch and line 7427 in that
boundary's CondFD/HAMT branch. Both calls require
`SurfExtCavityPresent(SurfNum)`. Window-class Surfaces, Surfaces
excluded by optional-Zone resimulation, every other boundary, and algorithms
outside those four cannot trigger CP176. A reached call nevertheless forwards
the cavity's complete raw `SurfPtrs` group, which can include
Windows or Surfaces outside the requested Zone.

The parent establishes a deliberately mixed timing boundary before CP176. It
has already zeroed the current Surface's exterior coefficients, applied four
EMS overrides through that Surface's `OSCMPtr`, copied the resulting
`HConv` to `SurfHConvExt`, and copied `TConv` to
local `TempExt`. CondFD/HAMT also copy their temperature, vapor,
mass-convection, and radiation boundary fields before CP176. CP176 then writes
the `OSCMPtr` stored on the cavity object. Neither CP176 nor
`GetHTSurfExtVentedCavityData` checks that this pointer equals every
member Surface's OSCM pointer.

For CTF/EMPD, line 7419 invokes CP175 after CP176 but passes the old local
`TempExt` and retains the old `SurfHConvExt`. When the two
OSCM pointers match, CP175 re-reads the newly written `TRad/HRad`,
so the current face solve mixes old convection with new radiation. The CP171
common tail likewise reads the new `TConv/HConv` only when those
pointers match. CondFD/HAMT retain
their fully pre-CP176 moisture-boundary snapshot for the current Surface, while
the common-tail report can still consume the new OSCM convection. If the
pointers differ, CP176 updates another OSCM and neither following helper is
required to consume that update.

The wrapper first performs these raw reads and calculations:


enumerated surrounding-surface factors into its own
`SurfsViewFactorSum`. `GetSurfaceLocalEnvData` then links pointers to numeric
Surfaces, copies that surrounding-only sum into
`Surface.ViewFactorSrdSurfs`, suppresses `SurfHasSurroundingSurfProperty`
when the copied sum is exactly zero, and enables the ground-property flags
whenever a ground pointer is present. Accumulated input errors fatal before
normal CP179 entry. Neither that linker nor CP179 itself enforces an
Outdoors boundary, heat-transfer status, or Surface class, and multiple
local-environment declarations can make different Surfaces share a mutable
surrounding or ground property record.

After both outer gates pass, CP179 visits numeric Surfaces 1 through
`TotSurfaces` and processes exactly those with
`SurfHasSurroundingSurfProperty` or
`IsSurfPropertyGndSurfacesDefined`. For each reached Surface it zeroes only
local accumulators; it does not reset any destination property or Surface
factor before reading live state. The read and sum order is:

1. If a surrounding property is present, read its sky value and presence
   flag. Add that sky value only when it is strictly greater than zero.
2. When no separate ground property is present, add the surrounding
   property's ground value unconditionally and use its ground presence flag.
   A separate ground property therefore takes precedence over this value.
3. Add every enumerated surrounding-surface factor from 1 through
   `TotSurroundingSurface`, without consulting the stored surrounding-only
   sum.
4. If a ground property is present, replace the selected ground flag/value
   with that object's flag and `SurfsViewFactorSum`, then add that complete
   sum.
5. When the resulting total is strictly greater than 1.0, emit one severe
   and one continue diagnostic. Do not set a local status, clamp, return, or
   skip the following writes.

The four presence-flag branches then execute in order:

- With both sky and ground set, overwrite `Surface.ViewFactorSkyIR` and
  `Surface.ViewFactorGroundIR` directly with the selected values. A total
  below one is not completed or normalized.
- With only sky set, overwrite sky with its selected value and ground with
  `1 - total`. A separate ground object has its set flag turned on and later
  reaches the reset child; without one, only the surrounding property's
  `GroundViewFactor` value is backfilled and its ground presence flag remains
  false.
- With only ground set, overwrite ground with its selected value and sky
  with `1 - total`. When a surrounding property exists, its sky value and
  presence flag are backfilled.
- With neither set, multiply the Surface's existing sky and ground IR factors
  separately by `1 - total`, preserving their prior ratio rather than
  splitting the remainder equally. A surrounding property receives the
  inferred sky value and flag and, when no separate ground object exists,
  the inferred ground value and flag. A separate ground object has its flag
  turned on and later reaches the reset child.

The invoked `ReSetGroundSurfacesViewFactor` body at lines 10074-10092 is
mapped separately by CP182 rather than folded into the CP179 routine row. It
first rechecks the Surface ground-property flag, replaces the property-wide
`SurfsViewFactorSum` with the newly assigned Surface ground IR factor, and,
when that replacement is exactly zero, disables the Surface ground
temperature and reflectance use flags and returns. Otherwise it writes the
entire replacement into `GndSurfs(1).ViewFactor`. It neither redistributes
the value across later entries nor clears them.

The property records are shared mutable inputs, so numeric Surface order is
observable. An earlier Surface can convert blank flags to set, replace a
ground-property sum and first entry, or backfill a surrounding-property
value before a later Surface reads the same record. Different initial
tilts or aliases can therefore make the first Surface's inferred split
control later Surfaces. Direct retry is not generally idempotent either.
In the valid sky-only path with no separate ground object, the first call
backfills a positive surrounding-property ground value but intentionally
leaves `IsGroundViewFactorSet` false. A second call while the latch remains
true includes that backfilled value in `total`, stays in the sky-only branch,
and can overwrite ground with zero; another unchanged call can restore the
remainder. Other inferred branches commonly convert both flags and settle
into the both-set branch, but CP179 has no local one-shot guard of its own.

The routine samples no schedules and changes neither
`Surface.ViewFactorSrdSurfs` nor the surrounding property's stored
surrounding-only sum. Later ground-reflectance and ground/surrounding
temperature helpers consume the property sums and schedules. Later in the
same `InitHeatBalance` startup path, `PerformSolarCalculations` can reach
`SkyDifSolarShading` when its BeginDay or detailed-integration caller gate
admits it; with `BeginSimFlag` still true, that child multiplies the new sky
IR factor by its diffuse-shading ratio and then rebuilds ground IR as the
complement, subtracting `ViewFactorSrdSurfs` when that flag is present.
CP179 is therefore the pre-shading initialization and property-backfill
step, not an isolated promise that its Surface factors are the final runtime
values.

without a separate ground object; SolarShading covers the inferred split
followed by diffuse shading; convection, Window, CTF, and Surface-manager

prefix, rollback, or retry. Every full-IDF fixture still invokes CP179
manually rather than proving the complete production startup path.

Beyond its one-sided aggregate-total diagnostic, CP179 performs no local
finite, sign, per-factor/lower-bound, index, dimension, count, allocation,
alias, topology, class, boundary, or lifecycle validation. It
has no status result, assertion, catch, rollback, cleanup, transaction, or
latch. A total above one continues into a negative-remainder write in the
three inferred branches; an explicit negative or nonfinite sky can be
excluded by the strict-positive sum test yet still be assigned when its flag
is true. Invalid surrounding/property indexing and an inconsistent
surrounding count can fail before the current Surface's first write while

owns the first-time latch. Clearing only that manager rearms CP179 against

`SurfaceProperty:GroundSurfaces`; no shared lists, explicitness flags,

CP180 first quick-returns when `AnyLocalEnvironmentsInModel` is false and

environments and local outdoor-air nodes can also make it true, so true can

After the global gate passes, the exact per-Surface work is:

1. Skip only when `IsSurfPropertyGndSurfacesDefined` is false. CP180 does not

   numerator.
6. If the completed numerator is exactly zero, write shared

   continue.
7. Otherwise write

   average. `root_4` is nested `sqrt`, so this is a radiative
   Kelvin-fourth-power average, not an arithmetic Celsius average. The success path does
   not write the Surface use flag.

The denominator is always the complete stored property sum. CP180 neither
subtracts view factors whose temperature schedules are null nor renormalizes
the remaining entries, so a blank-schedule entry can affect the result even

sums, or schedule values can propagate through the fourth-power/division/root
calculation without a diagnostic. A temperature of exact negative Kelvin with
otherwise positive factors contributes zero; malformed signed factors can
also cancel the numerator and take the disable branch.
