### CP182 `ReSetGroundSurfacesViewFactor` source map

CP182 maps non-required `ReSetGroundSurfacesViewFactor`, declared at
`HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.hh` line 216 and implemented at
`HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.cc` lines 10074-10092. Its only direct production
caller is `InitSurfacePropertyViewFactors` line 9989. The enclosing startup
path is `ManageHeatBalance` line 198 to `InitHeatBalance`, whose
`BeginSimFlag` block calls `InitSurfacePropertyViewFactors` at line 2623 after
`AllocateHeatBalArrays` and optional CTF initialization and before Window,
daylighting, and solar initialization.

CP182 itself has no model-wide, first-time, environment, day, timestep,
warmup, sizing, Surface-class, or boundary gate. It first tests only
`Surface(SurfNum).IsSurfPropertyGndSurfacesDefined` and returns without
following the property index or changing state when that flag is false.
Production nevertheless reaches the helper through stricter parent gates.
`InitSurfacePropertyViewFactors` returns unless
`AnyLocalEnvironmentsInModel` and its separately owned
`InitSurfaceHeatBalancefirstTime` latch are both true, then visits numeric
Surfaces having a surrounding or ground property. CP182 is requested only
when a separate GroundSurfaces property exists and the parent either finds a
stored sky factor but no ground factor or finds neither factor. Both-set,
ground-only, and no-separate-ground branches do not call it.

For either calling branch, the parent first determines and stores
`Surface.ViewFactorGroundIR`. It then sets the shared GroundSurfaces record's
`IsGroundViewFactorSet` true before invoking CP182. The helper neither infers
that factor independently nor writes the set flag; its standalone input is
the current Surface ground IR factor. In the normal authored blank-ground
case, input processing has left each entry factor at its default zero, so
backfilling the first entry usually makes the entry total match the newly
inferred denominator. CP182 does not check that precondition.

After the property-presence guard, the exact helper order is:

1. Follow `Surface.SurfPropertyGndSurfIndex` to the shared
   `GroundSurfsProperty` record.
2. Unconditionally overwrite `SurfsViewFactorSum` with the current
   `Surface.ViewFactorGroundIR`.
3. Compare the new shared sum exactly with zero.
4. On zero, write the current Surface's
   `UseSurfPropertyGndSurfRefl = false`, then
   `UseSurfPropertyGndSurfTemp = false`, and return.
5. On nonzero, copy the whole shared sum into only
   `GndSurfs(1).ViewFactor`.

The equality includes positive and negative zero. Negative finite values,
NaN, and either infinity bypass it and are copied to the first entry without
a warning or range check. The zero branch deliberately never accesses an
entry. The nonzero branch does not distribute the new sum across the list:
entry two and later retain their prior factors. CP182 also leaves the shared
temperature and reflectance averages, entry names and schedule pointers,
`NumGndSurfs`, `Surface.ViewFactorGroundIR`, and both use flags on the
nonzero path unchanged. It never enables a false use flag and never writes
`IsGroundViewFactorSet`.

These write boundaries make direct retries asymmetric. An unchanged nonzero
retry is overwrite-idempotent for the sum and first entry. A nonzero-to-zero
retry stores a zero denominator and disables both Surface use flags but
leaves the previous nonzero first entry stale. A zero-to-nonzero retry
refreshes the denominator and first entry without restoring either flag.
Pre-existing nonzero later entries can likewise make their total plus the
new first entry disagree with `SurfsViewFactorSum`. CP182 neither detects nor
repairs these states.

GroundSurfaces records may be shared by multiple Surfaces, while the two use
flags are Surface-local. During the normal numeric parent loop, the first
alias that encounters an unset blank ground factor sets the shared
`IsGroundViewFactorSet` flag and lets CP182 choose the shared denominator and
first entry. A later alias observes the already-set property and ordinarily
moves through a parent branch that does not invoke CP182, so the first alias's
value becomes order-visible shared input. Direct calls for multiple aliases always use last shared-sum write wins,
but only nonzero calls overwrite the first entry. A zero call preserves that
entry and disables only the calling Surface; a later nonzero alias cannot
re-enable it.

The shared values feed multiple later source-order consumers. A later CP179
parent entry can read the set flag and sum. CP181's reflectance helper reads
the sum and all entry factors during `InitSurfaceHeatBalance`, and CP180's
temperature helper does the same before outside-Surface work. Their
zero-denominator paths select global fallback by disabling the corresponding
Surface flag while preserving an earlier average; CP182 already disables
both flags on exact zero but does not clear either average. Input-created
output variables can therefore retain stale shared averages even though the
solver has selected fallback. Later solar shading can reconstruct
`Surface.ViewFactorGroundIR` without synchronizing CP182's property sum or
first entry, so these values are a startup snapshot rather than a permanent
two-way binding.

No test calls `ReSetGroundSurfacesViewFactor` directly. Four fixtures reach
it indirectly for six Surfaces:

- `HeatBalanceSurfaceManager_TestSurfPropertyViewFactorsInit` reaches the
  sky-only and neither-set branches for two Surfaces and asserts first-entry
  factors 0.2 and 0.3.
- `HeatBalanceSurfaceManager_TestSurfPropertySurfToGndLWR` reaches it once
  through the neither-set branch but asserts only Surface factors and
  downstream long-wave results.
- `HeatBalanceSurfaceManager_TestSurfPropertyViewFactorsReset` reaches the
  sky-only and neither-set branches for two Surfaces and again asserts
  first-entry factors 0.2 and 0.3.
- `SolarShading_TestSurfsPropertyViewFactor` reaches it once through the
  neither-set branch but asserts only parent and surrounding-factor results.

Five other focused parent fixtures have no ground property and never enter
CP182. The existing tests therefore cover only positive first-entry storage,
and directly check that field for four of the six reached Surfaces. They do
not directly assert the shared-sum assignment. The property quick return,
exact-zero branch and its write order, negative or nonfinite factors, a
greater-than-one parent total, empty or malformed entry storage, multi-entry
first-only behavior, shared aliases, standalone retry transitions, sticky
flags, diagnostics, failure prefix, or recovery remain untested.

Beyond the single property-presence and exact-zero checks, CP182 performs no
finite, sign, range, Surface-index, property-index, allocation, count,
dimension, alignment, topology, alias, or lifecycle validation. It emits no
warning, severe, status, or error flag and has no assertion, catch, rollback,
cleanup, transaction, or local latch. Input processing and the parent
normally establish valid indices and at least one entry, but those are
dependencies rather than helper enforcement.

An invalid Surface index can fail at the first guard before a local write. An
invalid property index can fail before the shared-sum assignment. With a
valid property but no accessible first entry, a nonzero call commits the new
sum and can then fail at `GndSurfs(1)`; a zero call avoids that access,
commits the sum, and clears both flags successfully. In a bounds-checked or
otherwise diagnosed execution, those committed prefixes and earlier
parent-loop Surface/property mutations remain if failure propagates. In a
release build, unchecked malformed access can be undefined and supplies no
deterministic prefix guarantee. From the production caller, the parent has
already stored the Surface ground factor and object set flag, and a
propagated failure prevents later Surfaces plus Window, daylighting, solar,
and the eventual first-time clear from being reached.

CP182 has no one-shot state of its own. The parent normally changes the
shared set flag before the first call, so same-state parent re-entry usually
selects a different branch and does not repeat CP182. `SurfacesData` owns the
Surface flags and factors plus the property arena; placement-new
`clear_state()` rebuilds that owner, and later Surface-property linking is
the ordinary path that sets both use flags true. The parent's first-time
latch belongs to separate HeatBalanceSurfaceManager state, defaults and
resets true, and clears only after successful `InitSurfaceHeatBalance`
completion. BeginEnvironment, day, hour, timestep, and ordinary retries do
not restore CP182 flags or reconcile the shared entry list. These separate
owners and parent writes do not form a transaction.

Rust has no typed `SurfaceProperty:LocalEnvironment`,
`SurfaceProperty:GroundSurfaces`, or
`SurfaceProperty:SurroundingSurfaces` arena; no shared property sum or
first-entry mutation; no per-Surface ground-property use flags; and no
matching parent branch, set-flag, alias, retry, or failure lifecycle. Ordinary
ground/sky view-factor helpers, the fixed 0.2 solar ground reflectance,
generic schedules, Ground/Foundation classifications, and run-blocked Zone
local-environment records are adjacent primitives only and do not implement
CP182.

### CP183 `GetSurroundingSurfacesTemperatureAverage` source map

CP183 maps non-required `GetSurroundingSurfacesTemperatureAverage`, declared
at `HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.hh` line 218 and implemented at
`HeatBalanceSurfaceManager.cc` lines 10094-10118. It immediately follows
CP182 `ReSetGroundSurfacesViewFactor` and is the final declared and defined
routine in the HeatBalanceSurfaceManager namespace; the header namespace
closes at line 220 and the translation-unit namespace closes at source line
10119.

Its sole direct production caller is unconditional
`CalcHeatBalanceOutsideSurf` line 7019. The parent first calls CP180 ground
temperature averaging at line 7016, then CP183, then begins internal-source
transfer at line 7023. Optional `ZoneToResimulate` handling does not begin
until lines 7041-7047, and the per-Surface Zone filter is later still. A CP180
nonreturn therefore blocks CP183, but every parent call that passes that
sibling reaches CP183 before full-model versus Zone-limited dispatch.

The ordinary `ManageSurfaceHeatBalance` path calls the parent at line 168.
Conditional final-radiant replay calls it at line 5216, and
`SimulationManager::Resimulate` calls it at line 2904. Chilled-ceiling,
electric, high-temperature and low-temperature radiant, hot-water and steam
baseboard, and ventilated-slab paths also invoke the parent, usually with a
Zone argument. Once any call enters the parent, CP183 itself is
unconditional. A Zone-limited radiant or HVAC retry still traverses all
eligible allocated Surfaces before the parent narrows later work.

CP183 first quick-returns when `AnyLocalEnvironmentsInModel` is false. It
does not clear existing averages on that path. When the gate passes, the
routine range-traverses the complete allocated `Surface` vector and skips
only a record whose `SurfHasSurroundingSurfProperty` flag is false. It does
not filter by numeric index, class, exterior boundary, heat-transfer status
or algorithm, Zone, Space, representative identity, timestep, environment,
sizing, warmup, kickoff, first-time state, or deduplication.

For each eligible Surface, the exact body is:

1. Zero local `SrdSurfaceTemp` and `SrdSurfaceTempSum` values.
2. Follow `SurfSurroundingSurfacesNum` to the shared
   `SurroundingSurfsProperty`.
3. Visit entries 1 through `TotSurroundingSurface` in stored order.
4. Unconditionally dereference the current entry's `tempSched`, call
   `getCurrentVal()` once, and add Kelvin. The getter selects `EMSVal` when
   actuated and `currentVal` otherwise.
5. Add `ViewFactor * pow_4(temperature + Kelvin)` to the local sum.
6. Divide the completed sum by the Surface-local cached
   `ViewFactorSrdSurfs`, apply `root_4`, subtract Kelvin, and assign the result
   to that Surface's `SrdSurfTemp`.

There is no zero-factor or null-schedule skip. A zero-factor entry still
samples and dereferences its schedule, so IEEE `0 * NaN` or `0 * infinity`
poisons the local sum. The denominator is not recomputed and CP183 never
reads the property's current `SurfsViewFactorSum`. Its only persistent write
is the final per-Surface average. It does not change the shared property,
entries, factors, count, cached denominator, presence flag, schedule
pointers, sky or ground state, diagnostics, or a shared average, and it
never disables a malformed Surface.

Normal input processing provides dependency guarantees that are not CP183
enforcement. `GetSurfaceSrdSurfsData` requires at least one complete
surrounding entry, requires matching extensible-field counts, allocates the
list, requires each entry temperature schedule to be nonblank and resolved,
and accumulates `SurfsViewFactorSum`. The v26.1 schema constrains each
individual surrounding factor to [0,1], but does not constrain their
aggregate to one. Local-environment linking copies that property sum into
`Surface.ViewFactorSrdSurfs` and clears
`SurfHasSurroundingSurfProperty` when the copied sum is exactly zero. Missing
property links or schedules become input errors and normally fatal before
simulation. CP183 rechecks none of this topology or arithmetic, and later
state mutation can make the Surface denominator disagree with the live
entry list.

With intended nonnegative factors and a positive cached denominator matching
their sum, line 10116 stores the radiative fourth-power mean in Celsius.
There is no equality, finite, sign, range, denominator, absolute-temperature,
or result check. All entries at exactly -273.15 C produce a stored -273.15 C
rather than a disable branch. Values below absolute zero have their Kelvin
sign erased by the fourth power. NaN schedules, factors, or denominators
propagate; positive overflow or division of a positive sum by positive zero
can store infinity; zero divided by zero and a negative quotient store NaN
through `sqrt(sqrt(x))`. None emits a CP183 diagnostic.

Multiple Surfaces can share one property. CP183 repeats every live schedule
read for each alias and stores a separate `SrdSurfTemp`. Aliases with matching
cached denominators receive the same stable result, while independently
mutated denominators can produce different results from the same numerator.
When multiple local-environment declarations target one Surface, input
linking overwrites its pointer and cache in declaration traversal order, so
the last matching declaration with a nonzero property pointer overwrites the
pointer and cache; an exact-zero copied sum keeps that last pointer cached but
disables the flag. Floating-point list
summation remains stored-order sensitive.

Stable schedules, entries, and denominator caches make successful retries
overwrite-idempotent. Current or EMS schedule changes are visible on the next
parent call. A false global gate or false per-Surface flag preserves the
previous `SrdSurfTemp` rather than zeroing it. There is no BeginEnvironment
reset of an existing average and no cursor or latch. `SurfaceData` defaults
the flag false and both `SrdSurfTemp` and `ViewFactorSrdSurfs` to zero;
`SurfacesData::clear_state` placement-news the owner and discards the arrays,
while later input and linking rebuild valid state. These owners and schedule
state do not form a transaction.

Three fixtures call CP183 directly:

- `ConvectionCoefficientsFixture.SurroundingSurfacesHRadCoefTest` writes two
  Surfaces having two entries each. It independently checks mixed-temperature
  radiative means near 10.80 C and 15.34 C and then checks

- `HeatBalanceSurfaceManager_SurroundingSurfacesTempTest` writes one Surface
  having three entries and checks exact equality against a test-side
  repetition of the same `pow_4`/`root_4` formula.
- `WindowManager_SrdLWRTest` writes one single-entry Surface at 25 C and
  checks the result only through Window surrounding long-wave output.

Those three calls write four property-bearing Surfaces and traverse eight

denominators, declaration overwrite order, zero entries, denominator/list

view-factor initialization helper; none proves standalone malformed-state

Beyond its global and per-Surface presence checks, CP183 performs no finite,

It emits no warning, severe, status, or error flag and has no assertion,

### CP184 `GetAirHeatBalanceInput` source map

`GetAirHeatBalanceInput(EnergyPlusData &state)` is declared at
`HeatBalanceAirManager.hh` line 67 and implemented at
`HeatBalanceAirManager.cc` lines 163-189. It is the first definition after
`ManageAirHeatBalance` lines 135-161 and immediately precedes
`GetAirFlowFlag` lines 191-214. Its only production call is the parent line
150 invocation under `ManageAirHeatBalanceGetInputFlag`.

The exact parent path is:

1. line 149 tests the caller-owned input flag;
2. line 150 calls CP184 when the flag is true;
3. only after normal return, line 151 writes the flag false;
4. line 154 calls `InitAirHeatBalance`;
5. line 158 calls `CalcHeatBalanceAir`; and
6. line 160 calls `ReportZoneMeanAirTemp`.

`ManageSurfaceHeatBalance` line 179 is the only production caller of that
manager. It reaches the Air subtree after complete outside and inside Surface
balance and before final Surface update and history work. On the ordinary
first simulation path, `GetHeatBalanceInput` and `InitHeatBalance` have
already run; `InitHeatBalance` under `BeginSimFlag` allocates the Zone heat
balance arrays that include false-initialized `ZoneMassBalanceFlag` records.
That broader setup is a dependency, not behavior owned by CP184.

CP184 creates `bool ErrorsFound = false` on every entry. It then executes,
without an intervening error test:

1. `GetAirFlowFlag(state, ErrorsFound)` at line 179;
2. `SetZoneMassConservationFlag(state)` at line 181; and
3. `GetRoomAirModelParameters(state, ErrorsFound)` at line 184.

Only after all three normally return does lines 186-188 inspect the shared
aggregate. A first-child error therefore does not suppress mass-conservation
or room-air input. A non-return from any child does suppress every later
child and CP184's final check. The middle child receives no error reference.
The room-air child creates its own local `ErrorsFound = false` and writes the
outer `errFlag` true only when its local processing failed; it never writes
the outer flag false. `GetSimpleAirModelInputs` likewise does not reset the
supplied reference. Thus normal-return aggregation is monotonic logical OR,
not last-child-wins status.

The wrapper's sole diagnostic is the line-187 terminal call

`GetAirHeatBalanceInput: Errors found in getting Air inputs`

through `ShowFatalError`. That helper does not return. CP184 does not test the
global severe-error count, so only child paths that set the shared boolean
reach this final fatal. For example, a missing required infiltration object
branch at lines 4168-4171 emits severe and continuation diagnostics without
setting the flag; by itself it does not satisfy CP184's predicate. Child
exceptions, invalid access, or other non-returns can escape before this
wrapper diagnostic.

The three child boundaries supply stateful context. CP185 and CP186 now
separately map the first and second children; CP185's complete parser remains
dependency context, as does the later room-air child:

- `GetAirFlowFlag` unconditionally writes `AirFlowFlag = true`, calls the
  complete simple-air-model input parser, then tests the populated
  infiltration, ventilation, mixing, cross-mixing, and refrigeration-door
  totals. When any total is positive it appends the `AirFlow Model, Simple`
  EIO record even if the returned shared error flag is already true. The
  parser allocates and populates airflow/report records, registers outputs,
  updates counts, and can emit warnings and severe diagnostics before
  returning.
- `SetZoneMassConservationFlag` runs next even after a returned airflow error.
  Only when mass balance is enforced and the adjustment mode is not
  `NoAdjustReturnAndMixing` does it visit expanded `ZoneMixing` records and
  set the receiving Zone flag before the source Zone flag. It clears nothing
  and reports no error. In direct or externally mutated CP186 state, a valid
  receiving endpoint followed by an invalid source can leave the receiving
  write committed; ordinary unresolved-source parsing can instead prevent
  CP185 from returning, and unchecked release access can be undefined.
- `GetRoomAirModelParameters` allocates the per-Zone AirModel array before
  validating all room-air declarations, populates model and global-use state,
  and writes the RoomAir EIO header and per-Zone rows before it propagates its
  local error to the outer aggregate. On error it first emits
  `Errors found in processing input for RoomAirModelType`, raises the outer
  flag, returns, and lets CP184 issue the terminal wrapper fatal.

CP184 itself performs no persistent domain-state assignment: its owned state
is the local boolean and final branch only. It validates no child pointer,
allocation, index, count, topology, duplicate, or lifecycle precondition and
has no catch, rollback, cleanup, transaction, compensating output, or local
one-shot guard. All returned-child allocations, flags, uniqueness state,
registered outputs, diagnostics, and EIO prefixes survive the final fatal.
A child non-return can retain an even shorter ordered prefix. The routine
offers no idempotence guarantee for direct or failed repeated entry.

`HeatBalanceAirMgrData::ManageAirHeatBalanceGetInputFlag` defaults true at
header line 101. `HeatBalanceAirMgrData::clear_state` resets it true and
clears `UniqueZoneNames` and `UniqueInfiltrationNames`, while `init_state` is
empty. The broader `EnergyPlusData::clear_state` also clears the child-owned
heat-balance and room-air state and is the supported clean retry boundary.
Clearing only the Air-manager data can therefore rearm CP184 while preserving
child allocations and effects.

On a successful production return the parent clears its flag before
initialization, calculation, or reporting. Every later manager call on that
state skips only CP184, even if one of those later children subsequently
fails. On CP184 fatal or any earlier non-return, the false assignment is not

present. A direct CP184 call never changes the parent latch. Consequently a
later manager call on the same uncleared state can execute the complete input
wrapper again. Repeated direct calls have no local skip and, when each child returns, revisit all three children.

### CP185 `GetAirFlowFlag` source map

`GetAirFlowFlag(EnergyPlusData &state, bool &ErrorsFound)` is declared at
`HeatBalanceAirManager.hh` line 69 and implemented at
`HeatBalanceAirManager.cc` lines 191-214. It follows CP184
`GetAirHeatBalanceInput` lines 163-189 and immediately precedes
`SetZoneMassConservationFlag` lines 216-233. Its sole production call is
CP184 line 179, where it is the unconditional first child before the
mass-conservation and room-air children.

The complete CP185-owned order is:

1. line 205 unconditionally writes
   `state.dataHeatBal->AirFlowFlag = true`;
2. line 207 unconditionally calls
   `GetSimpleAirModelInputs(state, ErrorsFound)`;
3. only after normal child return, lines 208-210 add the current
   `TotInfiltration`, `TotVentilation`, `TotMixing`, `TotCrossMixing`, and
   `TotRefDoorMixing` counts and compare the sum strictly greater than zero;
   and
4. a true comparison invokes one EIO `print` at lines 211-212.

CP185 never tests the prior `AirFlowFlag` value. A default false value and an
already true value both become true before input parsing. It does not clear
the selector for an empty model, an input error, a missing schedule, an
AirflowNetwork mode, or a zero summary count.

The passed `ErrorsFound` reference is transparent to CP185 itself. This
wrapper does not initialize, read, test, clear, or directly assign it, and it
does not early-return when the incoming value is already true.
`GetSimpleAirModelInputs` receives the same reference and has only monotonic
true assignments on its diagnosed paths. Therefore an incoming true remains
true, a clean child cannot clear an earlier error, and a child error can
return normally to CP185's count and output steps.

The child also contains severe paths that do not raise this boolean. A blank
`ZoneAirBalance:OutdoorAir` induced-air schedule emits
`ShowSevereEmptyField` at line 509 without an assignment, and a source-only
Mixing Zone missing its required Infiltration object emits severe and
continuation messages at lines 4168-4171 without an assignment. CP185 does
not inspect global severe counts or convert those diagnostics into status.
It emits no warning, severe, or fatal diagnostic of its own.

`GetSimpleAirModelInputs` is declared at header line 73 and spans source
lines 235-4244. That complete routine remains separate child dependency
context for CP185 and the next definition-ledger checkpoints. Relevant
effects include:

- lines 289-383 allocate Zone and optional Space air-report records and
  register baseline Zone, Space, and Site outputs;
- lines 429-639 process `ZoneAirBalance:OutdoorAir`;
- lines 641-1341 process the three `ZoneInfiltration` families;
- lines 1343-2416 process the two `ZoneVentilation` families;
- lines 2418-2922 process `ZoneMixing`, allocate mass-conservation state, and

- lines 2924-3451 combine explicit `ZoneCrossMixing` with generated

- lines 3453-3885 process `ZoneRefrigerationDoorMixing`;
- lines 3905-4154 emit detailed nominal-airflow EIO; and
- lines 4156-4238 publish Zone nominal totals, mass-conservation links, and
  related output registrations.

Thus CP185 delegates nine source input families:
`ZoneAirBalance:OutdoorAir`,
`ZoneInfiltration:DesignFlowRate`,
`ZoneInfiltration:EffectiveLeakageArea`,
`ZoneInfiltration:FlowCoefficient`,
`ZoneVentilation:DesignFlowRate`,
`ZoneVentilation:WindandStackOpenArea`, `ZoneMixing`, `ZoneCrossMixing`, and

identity, arrays, count production, diagnostics, output/EMS registration,

When the five-count sum is strictly positive, CP185 appends exactly:

```text
! <AirFlow Model>, Simple
 AirFlow Model, Simple
```

The detailed child EIO precedes this summary because the child must return
first. The output predicate excludes `TotZoneAirBalance`, so a model
containing only `ZoneAirBalance:OutdoorAir` leaves the selector true but emits
no CP185 summary. It also excludes EarthTube, CoolTower, and ThermalChimney
presence even though those later execute inside the selector-gated simple
airflow path. A positive sum writes the summary even when `ErrorsFound` is
already true; the EIO row is therefore neither proof of valid input nor proof
that CP184 will return. CP185 does not validate nonnegative count provenance,
sum range, output availability, or prior detailed-output success.

`AirFlowFlag` defaults false at `DataHeatBalance.hh` line 1865.
`GetAirFlowFlag` is its only source writer, and no source path writes it
false after CP185 runs. `HeatBalanceData::init_state` is empty;
`HeatBalanceData::clear_state` at lines 2051-2053 placement-news the complete
owner and restores the false flag, zero totals, and default arenas.

The flag has exactly two production read sites:

- `ZoneEquipmentManager::CalcAirFlowSimple` line 5643 returns when the flag is

ventilation, SQLite nominal data, mass conservation, Surface/CondFD nominal
airflow diagnostics, EMS, and output state. These consumers establish the

CP185 has no local guard, allocation check, pointer check, count validation,

When the child returns with the shared error true, CP185 can still append its

The first false-to-true flag write is stable on retry, but the complete call

registrations, detailed EIO, and the positive-count summary. Retained

`HeatBalanceAirMgrData::clear_state` rearms the manager latch and, among

Numerous tests call `GetSimpleAirModelInputs` directly and prove selected

### CP186 `SetZoneMassConservationFlag` source map

`SetZoneMassConservationFlag(EnergyPlusData &state)` is declared at
`HeatBalanceAirManager.hh` line 71 and implemented at
`HeatBalanceAirManager.cc` lines 216-233. It follows CP185
`GetAirFlowFlag` lines 191-214 and immediately precedes
`GetSimpleAirModelInputs` lines 235-4244 in definition order. Its sole
production call is CP184 `GetAirHeatBalanceInput` line 181, where it is the
unconditional second child after CP185 line 179 returns and before
`GetRoomAirModelParameters` line 184.

The complete CP186-owned order is:

1. line 226 reads
   `state.dataHeatBal->ZoneAirMassFlow.EnforceZoneMassBalance`;
2. only if that value is true, lines 226-227 read
   `ZoneFlowAdjustment` and compare it not equal to exact
   `DataHeatBalance::AdjustmentType::NoAdjustReturnAndMixing`;
3. only when both guards pass, line 228 visits integer indices 1 through the
   current `TotMixing` in ascending order;
4. for each record, line 229 writes
   `ZoneMassBalanceFlag(Mixing(Loop).ZonePtr) = true` for the receiving Zone;
   and
5. line 230 then writes
   `ZoneMassBalanceFlag(Mixing(Loop).FromZone) = true` for the source Zone.

The short-circuit order matters. A false enforcement flag never reads the
adjustment enum or any Mixing state. Exact no-adjust mode reads both controls
but writes nothing even when enforcement is true, including the
infiltration-only enforcement configuration produced by project-control
input. Any other enum representation passes the inequality if enforcement is
true; CP186 does not locally validate it. A zero or negative `TotMixing`
naturally visits no records. No branch clears or returns a flag value, status,
or diagnostic.

`GetProjectControlData` owns the controls. At
`HeatBalanceManager.cc` lines 1101-1193 it resets enforcement false, maps the
four active adjustment modes, defaults an invalid adjustment to no-adjust,
and can independently enable enforcement for added or adjusted infiltration.
That independence is why `EnforceZoneMassBalance == true` does not imply
CP186's loop will execute.

CP185's complete `GetSimpleAirModelInputs` child owns the expanded
`TotMixing` count and `Mixing` arena. Its lines 2418-2922 parse `ZoneMixing`,
resolve receiving `ZonePtr` and source `FromZone` endpoints, allocate
mass-conservation records, and compute `ZoneReOrder`. CP186 does not create,
resize, reorder, validate, or otherwise mutate those records. It uses only
`TotMixing` and `Mixing`:

- explicit `ZoneCrossMixing` is excluded;
- AirBoundary-generated cross mixing is excluded even though it contributes
  to `TotCrossMixing`;
- `ZoneRefrigerationDoorMixing` is excluded;
- infiltration and ventilation records are excluded; and
- Space identities are not represented in the output array.

Thus the active result is the union of Zone endpoints appearing in ordinary
expanded `ZoneMixing` records. Stored record order remains observable for
partial failure, but not in the final booleans after clean completion.
Duplicate endpoints repeat true writes. A self-mixing record writes the same
Zone twice, receiving first and source second.

On the ordinary production path, `InitHeatBalance` has already called
`AllocateHeatBalArrays` under `BeginSimFlag` before the Surface manager
reaches the Air manager. `AllocateHeatBalArrays` at
`HeatBalanceManager.cc` line 2875 dimensions one
`ZoneMassBalanceFlag` per Zone and fills every entry false. CP186 is the only
production writer that raises those entries true, and it never restores them
during the state lifetime.

The flag has four production read sites in two routines:

- `ZoneEquipmentManager::CalcZoneMassBalance` line 5056 reads it on each
  controlled-Zone visit of the mass-balance iteration loop before calculating
  incoming mixing and return flow;
  the result participates in mixing-source and receiving mass flows, return
  adjustment, infiltration treatment, iteration, and resimulation state; and
- `ZoneEquipmentManager::CalcAirFlowSimple` lines 6245, 6271, and 6295 read
  it in the negative, positive, and zero delta-temperature `ZoneMixing`
  branches. When the caller also requests adjusted mixing, a positive
  mass-balance-adjusted flow replaces the scheduled desired flow before heat,
  moisture, CO2, generic-contaminant, and reporting accumulations.

Those consumers establish state consequences, not numerical or output parity
claims for CP186. No other production read or true-write site exists.

CP186 receives no `ErrorsFound` reference, returns no status, and emits no
warning, severe, fatal, EIO, or other output. It does not inspect
`AirFlowFlag` or CP184's aggregate. Consequently a CP185 parser error that
returns normally still reaches CP186 with whatever complete parser state was

CP186 has no allocation, enum, count, array-length, index, Zone-range,
topology, duplicate, self-link, or result validation and no assertion, catch,
rollback, cleanup, transaction, or latch. Malformed direct or mutated state
has ordered prefixes:

- failure reading either guard leaves every prior flag unchanged;
- an invalid count or `Mixing` index can leave only earlier records committed;
- an invalid receiving `ZonePtr` can fail before the current record changes;
- a valid receiving endpoint followed by invalid `FromZone` can leave the
  receiving flag true; and
- unchecked release access can be undefined.

Normal input dependencies diagnose many endpoint errors before CP186. For
example, an unresolved source can leave `FromZone = 0` in parser state, but a
later parser dereference can itself prevent CP185 from returning. The
malformed-index prefixes above therefore describe direct or externally
mutated state, not a guaranteed ordinary-input continuation.

Stable valid repeated calls are value-idempotent because every write stores
true. The routine is not a topology-replacement transaction: a later false
guard, exact no-adjust mode, zero total, removed record, or changed endpoint
does not clear a Zone marked by an earlier call. Earlier and current true
writes also survive a later malformed access.

A CP186 non-return blocks the room-air sibling and CP184's aggregate fatal,
while `ManageAirHeatBalanceGetInputFlag` remains true because its clear
follows CP184's return. Same-state production retry therefore re-enters CP185
first and can then revisit CP186 with prior fan-system flags present.
Successful CP184 return clears only the parent latch and suppresses later
ordinary CP186 calls.

`HeatBalanceAirMgrData::clear_state` rearms that parent latch but does not

`EnergyPlusData::clear_state` followed by normal initialization is the clean

### CP187 `GetSimpleAirModelInputs` source map

`GetSimpleAirModelInputs(EnergyPlusData &state, bool &ErrorsFound)` is declared
at `HeatBalanceAirManager.hh` line 73 and implemented at
`HeatBalanceAirManager.cc` lines 235-4244. It follows CP186
`SetZoneMassConservationFlag` lines 216-233 and immediately precedes CP188
`GetRoomAirModelParameters` lines 4246-4492 in definition order. Its only
production call is CP185 `GetAirFlowFlag` line 207, after that wrapper
unconditionally writes `AirFlowFlag = true` and before CP185 inspects the five
summary counts.

CP187 is therefore a required child of required CP185 even though its ledger
position follows CP186. The source has no alternative production dispatch,
local first-call latch, early incoming-error return, final validation barrier,
or success result.

The complete major phase order is:

1. Lines 289-383 dimension local `RepVarSet` state and allocate `ZnAirRpt`.
   They allocate `spaceAirRpt` only for Space sizing or Space simulation, and
   register Space output variables only for Space simulation. The phase also
   registers the base Zone air-balance variables, optional advanced
   phase-change variables, six Zone exfiltration/exhaust variables, and two
   Site total-loss variables.
2. Lines 385-427 query maximum alpha and numeric argument widths across all
   nine direct schemas, then allocate shared alpha/numeric argument arrays,
   blank flags, and field-name arrays.
3. Lines 429-639 process `ZoneAirBalance:OutdoorAir`. The pass reads the raw
   object count, allocates the arena, resolves Zone/name/method/rates/schedules,
   writes each Zone's `zoneOABalanceIndex`, enforces uniqueness with
   `UniqueZoneNames`, handles hybrid-ventilation downgrade, sets the
   quadrature-use flag, and registers the combined-outdoor-air output family.
4. Lines 641-1341 process the three infiltration schemas in source order:
   `ZoneInfiltration:DesignFlowRate`,
   `ZoneInfiltration:EffectiveLeakageArea`, and
   `ZoneInfiltration:FlowCoefficient`. The setup helper expands eligible
   Zone/Space targets; the latter two models disallow both ZoneList and
   SpaceList expansion.
   CP187 sums the expanded counts into `TotInfiltration`, allocates one arena,
   populates each model's fields and report bindings, and registers the
   per-expanded-record outputs and EMS actuators.
5. Lines 1343-2416 process `ZoneVentilation:DesignFlowRate` and
   `ZoneVentilation:WindandStackOpenArea`. The design-flow family uses the
   shared expansion path, WindAndStack disallows list expansion, and the
   combined expanded count owns the ventilation arena. Parsing, schedules,
   model fields, outputs, and EMS registrations are completed before Mixing.
6. Lines 2418-2922 process `ZoneMixing`. The setup path disallows list
   expansion, populates receiving and source endpoints, schedules and model
   fields, and registers reports and EMS. Line 2831 then unconditionally
   allocates one `MassConservation` record per Zone. The following passes build
   per-Zone receiving/source Mixing-pointer arrays and fractions, participation
   flags, and `ZoneReOrder` in receiving-only, both-endpoint, then source-only
   order.
7. Lines 2924-3451 process `ZoneCrossMixing`. `TotCrossMixing` is the explicit
   expanded count plus `airBoundaryMixing.size()`. Explicit objects are parsed
   first; lines 3251-3268 append generated Construction:AirBoundary mixing
   records before output and EMS registration. AirBoundary is a dependency
   that contributes generated records, not a tenth direct parser schema.
8. Lines 3453-3885 process `ZoneRefrigerationDoorMixing`. The pass allocates
   per-Zone connection structures, resolves each paired endpoint, schedule,
   door geometry, and protection type, and registers its report and EMS state.
   The shared input scratch arrays are deallocated at lines 3887-3893.
9. Lines 3893-4159 emit the nominal-airflow EIO detail and form Zone totals.
   The routine visits infiltration, ventilation, Mixing, CrossMixing, and
   refrigeration-door records in family order and, only when
   `EnforceZoneMassBalance` is true, retains the last encountered per-Zone
   `InfiltrationPtr`. It writes `Zone.NominalInfilVent` and
   `Zone.NominalMixing`, and deliberately omits refrigeration-door flow from
   `TotMixingFlow`.
10. Lines 4161-4238 validate the infiltration dependency used by enforced
    Zone mass balance and register its mass-balance output family. Lines
    4240-4241 deallocate local total-flow arrays before the routine returns.

The direct input families are exactly nine:

- `ZoneAirBalance:OutdoorAir`;
- `ZoneInfiltration:DesignFlowRate`;
- `ZoneInfiltration:EffectiveLeakageArea`;
- `ZoneInfiltration:FlowCoefficient`;
- `ZoneVentilation:DesignFlowRate`;
- `ZoneVentilation:WindandStackOpenArea`;
- `ZoneMixing`;
- `ZoneCrossMixing`; and
- `ZoneRefrigerationDoorMixing`.

`TotZoneAirBalance` and `TotRefDoorMixing` follow their direct object counts,
while the other totals can include expansion or generated state as described
above. Auxiliary EarthTube, CoolTower, ThermalChimney, and AirflowNetwork
inputs are not CP187 parser families. CP187 also does not parse
`ZoneAirMassFlowConservation`; `GetProjectControlData` owns those controls.
It does not set CP185's `AirFlowFlag` and does not call CP186.

CP187 owns or mutates state across several persistent owners:

- `HeatBalanceData` owns report arrays, five CP185 summary counts plus
  `TotZoneAirBalance`, the family arenas, Zone nominal values, and
  `MassConservation`;
- `HeatBalFanSysData` owns `ZoneReOrder`;
- `HeatBalanceAirMgrData` owns the parent latch and uniqueness sets;
- OutputProcessor and EMS managers retain registrations and actuators;
- input and schedule managers provide resolved dependencies; and
- the EIO stream retains every successfully written row.

The routine constructs state incrementally. Earlier family allocations,
records, registrations, diagnostics, and EIO writes are not rolled back when a
later operation fails. Nominal EIO also contains source-sensitive unchecked
dependencies: an invalid Mixing source can remain `FromZone = 0` after its
diagnostic continuation and later be dereferenced in the Mixing row, and null
schedule state can likewise be read there. The enforced-mass-balance nominal
loop indexes `MassConservation` through each Infiltration record's `ZonePtr`.
Malformed state can therefore produce a diagnosed normal return, a non-return
with an ordered prefix, or unchecked release behavior; CP187 does not convert
those outcomes into one transactional status.

The supplied `ErrorsFound` reference is deliberately transparent:

- CP187 never initializes or clears it;
- an incoming true value does not suppress allocation, parsing, registration,
  nominal reporting, per-Zone writes, or the mass-balance tail;
- diagnosed source paths pass the reference onward or assign only true;
- CP187 never tests it and has no final fatal or return-status barrier; and
- after normal return CP185 still evaluates its positive five-count summary.

Two verified severe-diagnostic paths do not raise the reference. A blank
induced-air schedule in `ZoneAirBalance:OutdoorAir` emits
`ShowSevereEmptyField` at lines 508-510 without an assignment. Under enforced
mass balance, a source-only Mixing Zone with no Infiltration object emits its
severe and continuation messages at lines 4163-4172 without an assignment.
Either path can return with an incoming false reference still false. This also
means CP184's final fatal predicate is not equivalent to the global severe
count. Conversely, an error that CP187 does raise can return through CP185's
summary, after which CP184 still calls CP186 and room-air input before its one
final aggregate check. Any CP187 non-return prevents those later siblings.

There is no CP187-local retry protocol. On a normal first pass
`ZnAirRpt.allocate` is reached near the beginning, followed by many other
allocations and registrations. A direct same-state repeat normally encounters
already allocated arrays; if external mutation lets it continue, registrations
and EIO can repeat. `UniqueZoneNames` is populated by ZoneAirBalance and remains
in the Air manager until that owner is cleared, so clearing only HeatBalance
arrays can turn a retry into duplicate-name diagnostics. By contrast,
`UniqueInfiltrationNames` is only reserved here and is never inserted into or
read anywhere in this v26.1 routine.

Owner-local resets are insufficient:

- `HeatBalanceAirMgrData::clear_state` rearms the parent latch and clears the
  manager uniqueness sets but leaves HeatBalance, FanSystem, output, EMS, and
  EIO state;
- clearing only HeatBalance state leaves Air-manager uniqueness, `ZoneReOrder`,
  output, EMS, and EIO state; and
- a CP184 fatal after a normally returned CP187 error leaves the parent latch
  armed with the complete or partial child state still present.

A coordinated whole-`EnergyPlusData` reset followed by the normal input and
allocation sequence is the clean domain-state boundary. That reset does not
close or reset the EIO stream, so output-clean replay additionally requires a

### CP188 `GetRoomAirModelParameters` source map

`GetRoomAirModelParameters(EnergyPlusData &state, bool &errFlag)` is declared
at `HeatBalanceAirManager.hh` line 75 and implemented at
`HeatBalanceAirManager.cc` lines 4246-4492. It follows CP187
`GetSimpleAirModelInputs` lines 235-4244 and immediately precedes CP189
`InitAirHeatBalance` lines 4494-4507 in definition order. Its only production
call is CP184 `GetAirHeatBalanceInput` line 184, where it is the unconditional
third and final child after CP185 `GetAirFlowFlag` and CP186
`SetZoneMassConservationFlag` have returned.

CP188 is required even for an input with no `RoomAirModelType` objects. That
path still creates a default Mixing record for every Zone and writes the
RoomAir EIO header and one row per Zone. An error already returned by CP185
does not suppress CP186 or CP188; CP184 tests the shared aggregate only after
CP188 returns.

The routine has four ordered phases:

1. Lines 4268-4284 resize and default-fill `AirModel` to the current Zone count.
   Each `AirModelData` begins with an empty name and Zone name, `ZonePtr = 0`,
   model `Mixing`, coupling `Direct`, and `SimAirModel = false`. CP188 creates
   its own local `ErrorsFound = false`, counts `RoomAirModelType`, and raises
   that local error when the object count exceeds the Zone count without
   stopping later work. When at least one object exists, it dimensions
   `IsZoneDispVent3Node`, `IsZoneCrossVent`, and `IsZoneUFAD` to the Zone count
   with every value false; later settings readers, not CP188, set those arrays
   true.
2. Lines 4286-4450 read every `RoomAirModelType` in input order. The four alpha
   fields are authored object name, Zone name, model selector, and air
   temperature coupling. `NumNumbers` and `Status` are populated by
   `getObjectItem` but CP188 never tests them. Valid Zones receive the selected
   model, coupling, `SimAirModel` state, and global model-use flags; invalid
   Zones emit severe diagnostics and retain no object-specific Zone write.
3. Lines 4452-4467 visit every Zone regardless of object count or prior local
   error. They assign a synthetic record name and canonical Zone name, set
   `anyNonMixingRoomAirModel` true for every final non-Mixing selector without
   first clearing an earlier true value, and reject any non-Mixing model when
   either Space heat-balance simulation or sizing is active.
4. Lines 4469-4491 write the RoomAir EIO header and one row for every Zone in
   Zone order. Only after those writes does a local error emit
   `Errors found in processing input for RoomAirModelType` and assign the outer
   `errFlag = true`.

The sole direct parser schema is `RoomAirModelType`. Its model-specific actions
are:

| selector | CP188 state and dependency action |
|---|---|
| `Mixing` | performs no model-specific write or companion validation; on a fresh record the defaults remain Mixing and non-simulated |
| `OneNodeDisplacementVentilation` | sets `SimAirModel` and `DispVent1NodeModelUsed` true, then requires a `RoomAirSettings:OneNodeDisplacementVentilation` record whose `zone_name` matches |
| `ThreeNodeDisplacementVentilation` | sets `SimAirModel` and shared `UCSDModelUsed` true, then validates the matching `RoomAirSettings:ThreeNodeDisplacementVentilation` Zone |
| `CrossVentilation` | sets `SimAirModel` and `UCSDModelUsed` true, then validates the matching `RoomAirSettings:CrossVentilation` Zone |
| `UnderFloorAirDistributionInterior` | sets `SimAirModel` and `UCSDModelUsed` true, then validates the matching `RoomAirSettings:UnderFloorAirDistributionInterior` Zone |
| `UnderFloorAirDistributionExterior` | sets `SimAirModel` and `UCSDModelUsed` true, then validates the matching `RoomAirSettings:UnderFloorAirDistributionExterior` Zone |
| `UserDefined` | sets `SimAirModel` and `UserDefinedUsed` true but validates no temperature-pattern control or detail object here |
| `AirflowNetwork` | sets `SimAirModel` true and requires only that at least one `AirflowNetwork:SimulationControl` object exists |

The AirflowNetwork diagnostic says that intrazone nodes and linkages are needed
for a complete network, but CP188 does not inspect either family. Likewise,
`ValidateComponent` checks only whether the five named `RoomAirSettings:*`
schemas contain a record keyed by the same `zone_name`; it does not parse or
validate those records' remaining fields. `RoomAirSettings:AirflowNetwork`,
RoomAir nodes, temperature patterns, and all detailed settings belong to the
later lazy `RoomAirModelManager::GetAirModelDatas` pass.

An unknown model key maps to the invalid enum, emits warning and continuation
messages, and falls back to `Mixing` without raising the local error. An
unknown coupling key similarly warns and falls back to `Direct`. CP188 accepts
`Indirect` without additional validation. Explicit severe/local-error paths
are limited to:

- more `RoomAirModelType` objects than Zones;
- a Zone name that cannot be resolved;
- a selected OneNode, ThreeNode, CrossVent, UFAD Interior, or UFAD Exterior
  model without its same-Zone companion settings record;
- an AirflowNetwork selection with no `AirflowNetwork:SimulationControl`; and
- any final non-Mixing model combined with Space heat-balance simulation or
  sizing.

The source's apparent duplicate-Zone diagnostic does not protect a normal
entry. Line 4301 tests whether the current Zone's `AirModel.Name` is nonempty,
but the per-Zone arena was just default-filled and the object loop never stores
the authored object name. The first write to every record name occurs only in
the all-Zone tail at line 4454. Consequently, two or more declarations for one
Zone overwrite `ZoneName`, model, and coupling in input order without that
duplicate diagnostic.

The overwrite is not a clean last-record-wins transaction. A later `Mixing` or
invalid model does not clear `SimAirModel` that an earlier non-Mixing record set
true. Nor does it clear `DispVent1NodeModelUsed`, `UCSDModelUsed`, or
`UserDefinedUsed`. The final per-Zone enum and coupling can therefore disagree
with sticky per-Zone and global use flags. The separate object-count check can
still diagnose a total count above the Zone count, but it neither identifies
nor prevents the overwrite.

CP188 never preserves the authored `RoomAirModelType` object name. Instead the
tail writes `MIXING AIR MODEL FOR <Zone>` for every Zone, including Zones whose
final selector is non-Mixing, and overwrites `ZoneName` with the canonical Zone
name. `AirModelData::ZonePtr` is never assigned by this routine and remains its
default zero. The synthetic name, enum, coupling, and simulated flag can later
be serialized to SQLite; the EIO row instead uses the Zone name and a
model-specific display string.

Error propagation is deliberately local-to-outer and ordered:

- CP188 initializes only its local `ErrorsFound` false;
- it never reads, tests, or clears the caller's `errFlag`;
- an incoming true therefore does not suppress allocation, parsing, validation,
  default naming, Space checks, or EIO;
- a locally clean call leaves the outer reference unchanged and adds no CP188
  summary severe, even when it entered true;
- a local error does not suppress later objects, the all-Zone tail, or EIO;
- only after EIO does CP188 emit its summary severe and assign outer true; and
- an allocation, validation, formatting, EIO, or malformed-state non-return can
  leave an ordered state/diagnostic/output prefix before that outer assignment.

After a normal CP188 error return, CP184 immediately sees the shared true
aggregate and issues its terminal wrapper fatal. The parent manager clears its
input latch only after CP184 returns, so that fatal leaves the latch armed and
preserves CP185, CP186, CP188, diagnostic, and EIO effects for a same-state
retry.

CP188 owns no local latch, cleanup, rollback, transaction, or EIO reset. A
direct repeated call resizes and default-fills the per-Zone `AirModel` arena
again, but does not reset the monotonic model-use globals or
`anyNonMixingRoomAirModel` and writes another EIO header and Zone-row set.
Positive-object calls also false-dimension the three downstream Zone arrays
again; a later externally changed zero-object call does not enter that branch.

`RoomAirModelData::clear_state` clears the CP188 arena, the three Zone arrays,
`anyNonMixingRoomAirModel`, and the three global used flags. It does not rearm
the downstream room-air `GetAirModelData` or `MyOneTimeFlag` latches and does
not clear `MyEnvrnFlag`. The parent
`HeatBalanceAirMgrData::clear_state` separately rearms CP184's input latch.
`EnergyPlusData::clear_state` calls those owner-local clears but does not close
or reset the EIO stream. A fresh state, or explicit coordinated parent and
downstream room-air lifecycle rearming, is therefore needed for clean domain
replay; a fresh or explicitly reset EIO stream is additionally needed for
output-clean replay.

Principal source consumers include:

The Demand Manager reaches the second caller through

All domain mutation belongs to CP190 and its dependencies. `AirFlowFlag =

The fraction dependency has a material source quirk. For every
`MassConservation` record it reads `NumReceivingZonesMixingObject = N` but
never uses that Zone's `ZoneMixingReceivingPtr`. It zeros the record's first
`N` fractions, sums the global `Mixing(1..N).DesignLevel` prefix, and only when
that raw sum is strictly positive divides the same prefix by the sum.
Schedule- or EMS-scaled desired flows do not participate; zero, negative, or
NaN sums leave the touched fractions zero. This is bounded dependency context,
not a CP190 implementation or parity claim.

CP190 owns the full guards, traversal, arithmetic, fields, consumers, failure
prefixes, and repeated-entry behavior and remains the next checkpoint. CP189
neither improves nor weakens those semantics: every direct retry invokes the
child again. A normal repeat resamples schedules and EMS state and can restore
downstream-adjusted baselines, while false guards or shortened counts can
preserve untouched values. CP189 has no state of its own to clear.
`HeatBalanceData::clear_state` reconstructs the child-owned records, whereas
`HeatBalanceAirMgrData::clear_state` separately rearms the input lifecycle and
does not by itself undo those records. CP189 emits no EIO, so it adds no
output-stream reset requirement.

### CP190 `InitSimpleMixingConvectiveHeatGains` source map

`InitSimpleMixingConvectiveHeatGains(EnergyPlusData &state)` is declared at
`HeatBalanceAirManager.hh` line 79 and implemented at
`HeatBalanceAirManager.cc` lines 4509-4588. It follows CP189
`InitAirHeatBalance` lines 4494-4507 and immediately precedes CP191
`CalcHeatBalanceAir` lines 4590-4604 in source-definition order. The header
declares `initializeForExternalHVACManager` first at line 81, but that routine
is defined later at lines 4608-4613.

CP189 line 4506 is CP190's only literal production caller and invokes it
unconditionally exactly once per CP189 entry. CP189 is reached both from the
ordinary `ManageAirHeatBalance` line-154 path and from
`SimulationManager::Resimulate` line 2908 under `ResimHB`, so CP190 is required
for normal timestep initialization and for same-timestep demand-manager
resimulation.

Line 4527 first tests `state.dataHeatBal->AirFlowFlag`. A false value skips the
entire body and preserves every Mixing, mass-conservation, CrossMixing, and
refrigeration-door field. Normal production input reaches CP190 with the flag
true because CP185 `GetAirFlowFlag` writes it before parsing, but direct or
externally assembled state can select the complete no-op.

With a true flag, CP190 executes four ordered phases:

1. Lines 4529-4535 traverse the actual `Mixing` vector; `TotMixing` is not
   consulted. Each record first writes
   `DesiredAirFlowRate = DesignLevel * sched->getCurrentVal()`. The schedule
   getter returns its EMS value when schedule-level actuation is on. The
   schedule is still dereferenced when object-level EMS is already active. A
   true `EMSSimpleMixingOn` then replaces the product with
   `EMSimpleMixingFlowRate`, and the final desired value is copied to
   `DesiredAirFlowRateSaved`.
2. Lines 4539-4552 run only when
   `ZoneAirMassFlow.EnforceZoneMassBalance` is true and traverse the actual
   `MassConservation` vector. For each record they reset the local sum, read
   `NumReceivingZonesMixingObject = N`, and for Loop 1 through `N` first add
   global `Mixing(Loop).DesignLevel` and then zero
   `ZoneMixingReceivingFr(Loop)`. A sum strictly greater than zero triggers a
   second Loop 1 through `N` that divides those same raw global DesignLevels
   by the sum.
3. Lines 4555-4561 traverse the actual `CrossMixing` vector; `TotCrossMixing`
   is not consulted. Each record receives schedule times `DesignLevel` and
   then the same object-level EMS replacement. CP190 writes
   `DesiredAirFlowRate` only and does not update
   `DesiredAirFlowRateSaved`.
4. Lines 4567-4584 execute only when `TotRefDoorMixing > 0`, which is a
   boolean gate rather than the loop bound. `NZ` runs from 1 through
   `NumOfZones - 1` and directly indexes `RefDoorMixing(NZ)`. A false
   `RefDoorMixFlag` skips the record, and only `ZonePtr == NZ` enters its
   declared connections. Every reached `VolRefDoorFlowRate(J)` is first set
   to zero and then replaced with `EMSRefDoorFlowRate(J)` only when
   `EMSRefDoorMixingOn(J)` is true.

The mass-fraction phase intentionally does not use the current record's
`ZoneMixingReceivingPtr`. Every Zone therefore derives its first `N` weights
from the same global Mixing prefix even though
`CalcZoneMixingFlowRateOfReceivingZone` later applies those weights to that
Zone's pointer list. It also ignores the schedule- or EMS-scaled desired flow.
A raw sum equal to zero, negative, or NaN fails the strict positive test and
leaves all touched fractions zero. Negative DesignLevels may still produce
negative fractions when the total remains positive; infinities and NaNs are
not rejected. A zero or negative `N` naturally touches nothing, while an
oversized count can exceed either the global Mixing vector or the fraction
array.

The refrigeration-door phase does not sample `openScheds` or calculate the
physical door exchange. Its zero baseline lets later `CalcAirFlowSimple` use
the EMS volume directly or compute a non-EMS volume from the open schedule,
door geometry, protection factor, densities, and gravity. A false total gate,
`NumOfZones <= 1`, false record flag, Zone-index mismatch, or shortened
connection count leaves skipped state untouched.

Despite its name, CP190 writes no convective heat-gain accumulator. It also
does not process infiltration or ventilation, change any count, set Mixing or
CrossMixing `ReportFlag`, write `MixingMassFlowRate`, save CrossMixing flow,
gate on AirflowNetwork control, allocate arrays, validate topology, emit a
diagnostic or EIO row, return a status, or own a latch, catch, rollback,
cleanup, or transaction. The AirflowNetwork-versus-simple-flow selection
occurs later inside `CalcAirFlowSimple`.

Principal consumers are:

- `ZoneEquipmentManager::CalcAirFlowSimple` restores each active Mixing
  desired flow from CP190's saved baseline before optional mass-balance
  adjustment, computes Mixing and CrossMixing heat, moisture, contaminant, and
  Space/Zone terms, and consumes or replaces refrigeration-door volume;
- `CalcZoneMixingFlowRateOfReceivingZone` applies each CP190 fraction to the
  Mixing object selected by that Zone's receiving-pointer list; and
- `HVACManager::ReportAirHeatBalance` uses Mixing and CrossMixing desired
  volume plus refrigeration-door volume for mass, sensible, latent, and
  volumetric reports.

CP190 has no local failure conversion. A null schedule or schedule-getter
non-return happens before the current Mixing assignment, even when that
record's object-level EMS override is active. In a fraction first pass, a
Mixing read fails before the current fraction is zeroed, whereas a fraction
write fails after the current raw DesignLevel has entered only the local sum;
a normalization failure can retain a normalized prefix and zero tail. Invalid
vector/count alignment, missing Zone-indexed door records, or malformed
connection arrays can likewise stop execution, and a door EMS flag or rate
failure can follow the current connection's committed zero. The persistent
prefix follows source order: completed Mixing records first; then completed
fraction records and elements; then completed CrossMixing records; then prior
door records and connections. Later CP189 callers and reports are suppressed
according to the CP189 caller boundary.

A normal repeated call resamples current schedule-level and object-level EMS
state, restores `DesiredAirFlowRateSaved` from the new Mixing baseline,
zeroes and rebuilds every reached fraction range, recomputes CrossMixing
desired flow, and resets reached non-EMS door volumes to zero. This is the
intended same-timestep `Resimulate` path. It is not a global cleanup:
`AirFlowFlag = false`, disabled mass balance, a nonpositive door total, skipped
door records, or shortened counts retain untouched prior state.

`HeatBalanceData::clear_state` placement-new reconstructs `AirFlowFlag`,
counts, vectors, fraction records, EMS fields, and door arrays.
`HeatBalanceAirMgrData::clear_state` separately rearms CP184's input latch and
clears parser uniqueness state but does not reset CP190-owned records. A clean
production replay requires coordinated clearing and normal reinitialization
of HeatBalance, Air-manager, FanSys consumer, and Schedule state. CP190 emits
no EIO or other output, so it adds no output-stream reset requirement.

### CP194 `calcMeanAirTemps` source map

`calcMeanAirTemps(EnergyPlusData &state, Real64 const ZTAV,
Real64 const airHumRatAvg, Real64 const MRT,
DataHeatBalance::AirReportVars &thisAirRpt, int const zoneNum)` is declared at
`HeatBalanceAirManager.hh` lines 87-92 and implemented at
`HeatBalanceAirManager.cc` lines 4689-4728. The namespace and file end at line
4730, so CP194 closes the HeatBalanceAirManager definition order.

Both literal callers belong to CP193 `ReportZoneMeanAirTemp`. Line 4678 calls
CP194 once for every `ZoneLoop = 1..NumOfZones` with that Zone's `ZTAV`,
`airHumRatAvg`, `MRT`, `ZnAirRpt` record, and Zone number. Lines 4682-4683 call
it for each stored Space membership when Space heat-balance simulation is
active. A Space supplies its own three averaged values and `spaceAirRpt`
record, but CP193 deliberately passes the owning `ZoneLoop` as `zoneNum`.
There are no other production or test calls. Because every ordinary completed
Air-manager traversal delegates its Zone and active-Space report-field
calculation here, CP194 is required for the full-domain inventory.

The body performs this ordered write and dependency sequence:

1. Line 4699 writes `MeanAirTemp = ZTAV`. This is the Zone or Space average of
   system-timestep air temperatures over the Zone timestep, not a fresh
   instantaneous MAT.
2. Line 4700 copies raw `airHumRatAvg` into `MeanAirHumRat`.
3. Line 4701 writes ordinary `OperativeTemp = 0.5 * (ZTAV + MRT)`.
4. Line 4702 evaluates
   `Psychrometrics::PsyTdpFnWPb(state, MeanAirHumRat, OutBaroPress)` and writes
   the returned dew point.
5. Lines 4706-4722 can read operative-control state and update
   `ThermOperativeTemp`.
6. Lines 4723-4727 can evaluate the wet-bulb dependency and update
   `WetbulbGlobeTemp`.

The thermostat-operative branch requires all three source guards:
`AnyOpTempControl`, `Zone(zoneNum).IsControlled`, and the referenced
`TempControlledZone.OpTempCtrl != None`. Line 4708 reads
`TempControlledZoneIndex` before checking `IsControlled`, although the control
array is not indexed until after the check. Exact `Scheduled` mode alone reads
`opTempRadiativeFractionSched->getCurrentVal()`; that schedule accessor returns
`EMSVal` while actuated and otherwise `currentVal`. Every other non-`None`
mode, including the ordinary `Constant` value and any malformed non-`None`
enum, takes `FixedRadiativeFraction`. CP194 provides no index, pointer,
finite-value, or `[0,1]` validation. It then redundantly restores the same
50/50 ordinary `OperativeTemp` and writes
`ThermOperativeTemp = (1-f) * ZTAV + f * MRT`, so an unrestricted fraction can
extrapolate. If any guard is false, `ThermOperativeTemp` remains at its prior
or default value rather than being reset to ordinary operative temperature.

`PsyTdpFnWPb` at `Psychrometrics.hh` lines 1529-1552 applies
`W0 = max(W, 1e-5)` only inside the child, computes
`PDEW = PB * W0 / (0.62198 + W0)`, and delegates to `PsyTsatFnPb`. Thus the
stored `MeanAirHumRat` is never clamped. The default raw saturation miss path
bounds dew-vapor pressure at approximately `-100 C` below `0.0017 Pa` and `200 C` above
`1555000 Pa`, has a special freezing interval, otherwise iterates at most 50
times, and can emit non-warmup psychrometric warnings while still returning a
value. The optional performance interpolation mode follows a different
spline path, so raw-miss boundary behavior is dependency context rather than
an unconditional CP194 formula.

When `ReportWBGT` is true, lines 4725-4726 compute

`WetbulbGlobeTemp =
0.7 * PsyTwbFnTdbWPb(state, ZTAV, airHumRatAvg, OutBaroPress)
+ 0.3 * OperativeTemp`.

The child receives the raw averaged humidity ratio. The final term is always
the ordinary 50/50 operative value, never `ThermOperativeTemp`. The raw
wet-bulb routine corrects negative humidity locally, can warn for sufficiently
negative humidity, out-of-range dry bulb, or nonconvergence, iterates at most
100 times, returns its current result after warning, and finally enforces
`TWB <= TDB`. CP194 itself checks none of the temperature, humidity, pressure,
iteration, denominator, NaN, or infinity conditions. A false `ReportWBGT`
preserves the prior/default WBGT field.

The pinned v26.1 default build enables psychrometric caching and errors while
statistics are off. Saturation and wet-bulb caches use truncated input-bit
tags; a wet-bulb miss reconstructs the truncated values for raw calculation,
so nearby inputs can share a cached result. Fresh zero tags can appear as
initialized false hits, prior collisions/history can affect the selected slot,
and a miss records tags before raw work returns. The dependencies can also
mutate saturation pressure memo, wet-bulb boiling-pressure memo, warning and
recurring-error indices/streams, and optional call statistics.
`PsychrometricCacheData::clear_state` resets statistics and saturation
precision but does not invalidate all cached arrays, while
`PsychrometricsData::clear_state` resets warning indices and its raw
memo/settings. These effects prohibit describing the whole CP194 call as a
pure calculation or promising cold retry merely because its report-field
assignments are overwrite-shaped.

1488-1489. Zone and Space report vectors live at lines 2031-2032.

operative temperature, dew point, and humidity ratio at

1668-1675 and 1737-1744 separately bind controlled-Zone
`ThermOperativeTemp`; CP194 can calculate the Space field, but the generic

CP194 emits no ESO, SQL, EIO, or diagnostic directly. OutputProcessor and EMS
observe the bound records later.

CP194 owns no allocation, bounds/null/finite validation, return status,

A normally returned repeat overwrites the first four fields from current
inputs and resamples scheduled/EMS control state. `ThermOperativeTemp` and

`EnvironmentData::clear_state` owns pressure, and the two psychrometric owners
hold the dependency lifecycle. Resetting only an `AirReportVars` record or the
Air-manager owner is therefore not a clean whole-state replay.

`PredictSystemLoads(EnergyPlusData &state, bool ShortenTimeStepSys,
bool UseZoneTimeStepHistory, Real64 PriorTimeStep)` is declared at
`ZoneTempPredictorCorrector.hh` lines 276-280 and implemented at
`ZoneTempPredictorCorrector.cc` lines 2870-3145. Its only production call
expression is CP195 `ManageZoneAirUpdates` line 227 under the `PredictStep`
selector. It is reached only after the wrapper's optional CP196 input and
unconditional CP199 initialization return, receives all three timestep
arguments unchanged, and never receives or alters caller-owned
`ZoneTempChange`.

Three production PredictStep entrances share that expression:

| Entrance | Immediate source order and arguments |
|---|---|
| `HVACManager` lines 262-267 | after setpoint acquisition, airflow/AFN, lagged dependent loads, indoor-green, and internal-gain updates; before `SimHVAC`; the initial path has `ShortenTimeStepSys = false`, `UseZoneTimeStepHistory = true`, and `PriorTimeStep = TimeStepZone` |
| `HVACManager` lines 346-351 | only inside `TimeStepSys < TimeStepZone` substeps; adaptive downstepping makes the first call shortened with Zone history disabled, then line 372 clears shortening so later substeps can call with false/false while retaining the prior Zone timestep |
| `SimulationManager::Resimulate` lines 2929-2930 | under `ResimHVAC`, after Get setpoints and simple airflow and before `SimHVAC`; passes false shortening, the current history selector, and zero prior timestep |

CP202 then executes four ordered phases.

#### Staged thermostat phase

When `NumStageCtrZone > 0`, lines 2915-2992 walk exactly that many
`StageControlledZone` records in stored order. Each record trusts
`ActualZoneNum`, both schedule pointers, the stage counts and offset arrays,
Zone/Space membership, and all destination arrays. It samples both base
schedules on every call and overwrites `HeatSetPoint` and `CoolSetPoint`.
`ZoneT` is the Zone record's `MAT`, replaced by `XMPT` only when shortening.

If sampled heating is greater than or equal to cooling, CP202 increments
`StageErrCount`. The first occurrence emits a warning, continuation, and
timestamp; every later occurrence updates a recurring warning using
`StageErrIndex` and the sampled heating value as both tracked extrema. It then
sets heating to cooling minus 0.1 C and performs no second validity check.

| Mode selection | `StageNum` and thermostat setpoint writes |
|---|---|
| strict `CoolSetPoint < ZoneT` | offset is `ZoneT - CoolSetPoint`; the last index whose offset is greater than or equal to `CoolTOffset(I)` wins as negative `-I`; both high and low become cooling minus half `CoolThroRange` when offset reaches that half range, otherwise cooling plus that half range |
| otherwise strict `HeatSetPoint > ZoneT` | offset is `ZoneT - HeatSetPoint`; the last index whose absolute offset reaches the absolute `HeatTOffset(I)` wins as positive `I`; both low and high become heating plus or minus half `HeatThroRange` |
| otherwise | high becomes cooling plus half `CoolThroRange`, low becomes heating minus half `HeatThroRange`, and `StageNum = 0` |

The heating half-range decision at line 2973 intentionally compares the
absolute offset with half `CoolThroRange`, not `HeatThroRange`, although the
assigned displacement uses `HeatThroRange`. This source-literal asymmetry is
part of the map. After each staged Zone, `doSpaceHeatBalance` copies its final
`StageNum` to every stored Space demand membership; simulation and sizing modes
both qualify.

#### On/off cutout prefix

`NumOnOffCtrZone > 0` is only an outer gate. Lines 2999-3111 still scan all
`NumTempControlledZones` and process every record whose `DeltaTCutSet > 0`.
A shortened call restores `HeatModeLast` and `CoolModeLast` from their saved
values; a nonshortened call first saves the current values. It then clears both
off flags. ThirdOrder selects `MAT`, or `XMPT` when shortened, as `Tprev`;
Analytical, Euler, and every other algorithm use `T1` regardless of shortening.

The fixed tolerance is 0.02 C, and the implementation preserves its literal
strict comparisons:

| Control type | Revision and mode-memory override |
|---|---|
| `SingleHeat` | initialize generic and low setpoints to base low; write base low plus delta when `Tprev < low + 0.02` or when `Tprev > low && Tprev < low + delta - 0.02`, otherwise set `HeatOffFlag`; prior heat mode with `Tprev > low` overrides back to base and sets the off flag |
| `SingleCool` | initialize generic and high setpoints to base high; write base high minus delta when `Tprev > high - 0.02` or when `Tprev < high && Tprev > high - delta + 0.02`, otherwise set `CoolOffFlag`; prior cool mode with `Tprev < high` overrides back to base and sets the off flag |
| `DualHeatCool` | initialize high and low separately, run the same cooling logic first and heating logic second, and do not write the generic `setpt` member |
| `SingleHeatCool`, Uncontrolled, and every other value | no switch-owned setpoint write; the preceding save/restore and off-flag clears still persist |

After both DualHeatCool halves, an inclusive `setptLo >= setptHi` test emits a
severe diagnostic, a timestamp naming the Zone, two formatted setpoint
continuations, and a fatal. The diagnostic occurs after all already reached
staged and on/off mutations and before any Zone load child.

#### Zone and Space child dispatch

Lines 3114-3126 always visit `zoneNum = 1..NumOfZones`. Each Zone first calls
the next source definition, CP203
`ZoneSpaceHeatBalanceData::predictSystemLoad`, with the three original
timestep arguments and `zoneNum`. Its temperature/history update, coefficient,
sensible demand, and moisture demand calculations remain CP203 dependency
behavior rather than CP202 implementation credit.

The current Zone's `spaceIndexes` are then visited in stored order:

| Space condition | CP202 action |
|---|---|
| `doSpaceHeatBalance` | call CP203 on `spaceHeatBalance(spaceNum)` with the same arguments plus `zoneNum` and `spaceNum` |
| inactive Space heat balance and shortened call | copy only the already processed Zone `MAT` and `airHumRat` to that Space record |
| inactive Space heat balance and nonshortened call | leave the Space record unchanged |

Zone and Space work is interleaved per Zone. `UseZoneTimeStepHistory` and
`PriorTimeStep` are not otherwise read by CP202. Counts, indices, duplicate
memberships, array shape, and identity consistency are not locally reconciled.

#### Final on/off memory phase

Only after every reached child returns do lines 3127-3144 rescan positive
cutout controls. Cooling last-mode memory becomes exactly
`CoolOffFlag && TotalOutputRequired >= 0`; heating becomes exactly
`HeatOffFlag && TotalOutputRequired <= 0`. The inclusive tests allow both to
be true at zero when both off flags are true. A NaN load makes both comparisons
false. Controls skipped by the positive-delta predicate retain their prior
mode fields.

CP202 owns no latch, status result, finite/sign/range validation, catch,
cleanup, or rollback. NaN schedule or temperature comparisons follow native
false branches, can select staged deadband or off flags, and can bypass the
dual collision; infinities and unusual ranges propagate through arithmetic.
Null schedules, invalid actual Zone numbers, short stage arrays, malformed
demand arrays, and bad Space memberships reach unchecked dependency or
container behavior.

A dual fatal retains the complete staged phase plus the reached on/off
save/restore, off-flag, and setpoint prefix, and suppresses every child and the
final mode pass. A Zone or Space child non-return retains all earlier
Zone/Space effects and fallback copies and likewise suppresses the remaining
tail. Same-state retry samples schedules again, increments staged error state
again, may replace saved mode state, and repeats child effects. A clean replay
requires coordinated reconstruction of predictor counts and Zone/Space
records, ZoneControls staged and temperature records, HeatBalFanSys setpoints
and control types, ZoneEnergyDemand stages and loads, HeatBalance topology,
HVAC timestep/history state, diagnostic recurrence state, and CP203's
dependencies. Clearing only one owner can leave stale counts, indices, or
state in another.

Search finds exactly 16 direct CP202 calls in two fixtures:

- `SetPointWithCutoutDeltaT_test` makes eight nonshortened Euler calls.
- `TempAtPrevTimeStepWithCutoutDeltaT_test` makes four normal and four
  shortened ThirdOrder calls, using `MAT` versus `XMPT` and saved last modes.
- Together they assert 24 low/high setpoint values across two SingleHeat, two
  SingleCool, one SingleHeatCool, and three DualHeatCool calls per fixture.

Both fixtures pass false `UseZoneTimeStepHistory` and 0.01 prior time and leave
global `NumOfZones` at zero. They therefore execute the on/off prefix and final
mode loop but no Zone/Space CP203 child. They assert no off flags, saved or
final modes, staged thresholds or diagnostics, exact 0.02 boundaries, dual
fatal, argument forwarding, Space branch, partial failure, retry, or reset.

Of 57 active C++ `ManageSimulation` calls, one EMS callback test fatals before

`WeatherManager_SetRainFlag` case executes no Zone child, while 55 execute at
